Abstract:Understanding holistic 3D human motion and the surrounding environment from egocentric video is fundamental for applications in AR/VR and robotics. Although these tasks are inherently coupled, existing methods treat them separately. In particular, egocentric motion reconstruction methods typically assume access to metric, gravity-aligned camera trajectories from specialized inertial sensors. Recovering such trajectories from monocular egocentric video remains a significant challenge due to rapid head movements and motion blur. We present EgoMo3R, a joint optimization framework that simultaneously reconstructs 3D human motion and scene geometry from casual egocentric video. It leverages the robustness of low-level visuo-geometric primitives, including monocular depth, optical flow, and point tracks, integrated with a diffusion-based human motion prior via first-order optimization. We propose an alternating optimization scheme that establishes a synergistic feedback loop: scene reconstruction provides physical grounding and trajectory conditioning for the motion prior, while the motion prior regularizes the camera trajectory and anchors the scene in a metric, gravity-aligned world frame. We evaluate EgoMo3R on the highly dynamic sequences of the EgoExo4D and Nymeria datasets and show that it outperforms specialized baselines in both 3D scene reconstruction and egocentric motion estimation.

[CV-181] Special and General Computational Aesthetics

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01626
作者: Ganqing Luo(1 and 2),Chuan Li(1),Liaoruxing Zhang(3 and 5),Xin Jin(4 and 5) ((1) Sichuan Fine Arts Institute, Chongqing, China, (2) Chongqing College of Artificial Intelligence, Chongqing, China, (3) Beihang University, Beijing, China, (4) Beijing Electronic Science and Technology Institute, Beijing, China, (5) State Key Laboratory of General Artificial Intelligence, Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence (BIGAI), Beijing, China)
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)
备注: 18 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Presented at the 2026 CCF Chinese Conference on Computational Art (CCAC 2026), Jinan, China, October 2026; to appear in the conference proceedings

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Computational aesthetics is a field at the intersection of computer science, artificial intelligence, aesthetics, and other disciplines. As AI has developed, the field has formed relations of inclusion, intersection, or support with computational art, AI art, AI aesthetics, AI-generated content (AIGC), computational creativity, affective computing, and neuroaesthetics. Without distinguishing scope, objectives, and methods, it may be narrowed to image aesthetic quality assessment or expanded into an umbrella term for AI’s involvement in art. We analyze its internal structure and its relations with neighboring concepts, and propose a two-level scope: special computational aesthetics (SCA) and general computational aesthetics (GCA). SCA centers on aesthetic measurement and aesthetic process modeling. The former primarily corresponds to “Aesthetic Perception”: computationally identifying and representing aesthetic attributes and predicting human aesthetic evaluations; the latter primarily to “Aesthetic Understanding”: computationally describing, testing, and explaining how human aesthetic perception and judgment are formed. GCA extends this core to include “Aesthetic Generation,” namely artistic generation guided by computational aesthetic models. Some computational aesthetic tasks can also use non-AI methods. Research in this scope using AI algorithms and models we define as AI aesthetics, which may involve the special core and the general extension. “Aesthetic Generation” intersects with AIGC, AI art, and computational creativity, but belongs to the general extension defined here only when computational aesthetic models substantively constrain, guide, or optimize artwork generation. We also draw on Feng Peng’s discussion of the computability of beauty, aesthetic experience, and art as a theoretical reference for clarifying boundaries between computational aesthetics and related concepts. Comments: 18 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. [CV-182] Seeing What Matters Verifying What Pays: Load-Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01617
作者: Hong Nie,Zhangchi Gao,Yuqian Liang,Jun Yu,Bo Wang,Jianqing Sun,Shengping Liu
类目: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Speculative decoding accelerates vision-language model (VLM) inference without altering the output distribution, yet two factors limit its gains. Existing drafters either lack the image evidence required for visually grounded tokens or pay to condition on every visual token, although a short draft block typically depends on only a few image regions. Moreover, the value of verifying additional candidates varies with GPU load, so no fixed verification structure is efficient across serving conditions. We present Uni-LaSpec, a block-parallel speculative decoding framework that addresses both factors. To improve draft quality, Uni-LaSpec reuses the verifier’s own attention: the query retained from the preceding verification ranks the cached, int8-quantized visual keys, and a cross-layer vote selects a few visual tokens that the drafter fuses through gated cross-attention. Acceptance-aware training further weights each draft position by its contribution to the accepted prefix. To allocate verification, a marginal-cost criterion selects the structure per request and per round: draft trees exploit idle verifier capacity under light load, whereas a dynamic head truncates linear drafts under heavy load. Across six VLMs from three model families and 17 text and multimodal benchmarks, selecting eight visual tokens retains at least 98.6% of the acceptance obtained from the full image at sub-millisecond selection cost. With greedy decoding at concurrency one, Uni-LaSpec achieves up to 5.11x text and 3.24x multimodal throughput over autoregressive decoding. Across six load levels and three GPU types, it outperforms autoregressive decoding in every setting and matches or exceeds the best fixed verification strategy in 123 of 144 settings; under bursty arrivals, it reduces mean end-to-end latency by 47.6% relative to linear verification.

[CV-183] NatureFusion: Rethinking Infrared and Visible Image Fusion as Natural Complementary Enhancement

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01607
作者: Jianfeng Ding,Linfeng Tang,Hao Zhang,Han Xu,Xunpeng Yi,Yibing Zhang,Meiqi Gong,Zhongyuan Wang,Jiayi Ma
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 17 pages, 13 figures, 12 tables

点击查看摘要

Abstract:In the absence of ground truth, most existing infrared and visible image fusion methods pursue fidelity to the source images and directly superimpose two physically distinct modalities. As a result, salient infrared targets appear as bright patches of thermal radiation pasted onto the scene. These patches obscure the original color and texture of the targets, so the fused images look unnatural to human observers and deviate from the data distribution learned by vision models pretrained on visible images. Therefore, we redefine infrared and visible image fusion as natural complementary enhancement rather than source fidelity, and propose NatureFusion, which exploits cross-modal complementary cues to infer a clear and natural visible-style image from low-quality visible and infrared image pairs. Specifically, to address the lack of ground truth, we employ a generative foundation model as the teacher to directly generate visually natural fused images for supervision. Furthermore, to fully distill the teacher’s generative capability while reducing computational cost, we fine-tune a pretrained generative model with conditional flow matching through a light-weight fusion adapter. Last but not least, to further improve downstream performance without sacrificing natural appearance, we freeze the fusion adapter and introduce a detector-supervised task adapter that strengthens the complementary contribution of infrared. Extensive comparisons with seven multi-modal fusion and seven single-modality enhancement methods demonstrate that NatureFusion generates visually natural fused images with the best perceptual quality. Detection and segmentation models pretrained on visible images achieve substantially higher accuracy on our fused images than on those of any competing method.

[CV-184] MedNet and U2-ViT: A Nested Vision Transformer Diffusion Framework for Diverse Medical Images Generation

作者: Lakshmikar R. Polamreddy,Jialu Li,Youshan Zhang

Abstract:The scarcity of diverse, high-quality medical images remains a significant bottleneck in advancing AI-driven medical diagnostics and treatment planning. Traditional datasets often suffer from class imbalances, limited disease coverage, and insufficient variations in imaging conditions - challenges that hinder the development of robust, generalizable models. To address this, we introduce MedNet, a large-scale, multi-modal text-to-image dataset spanning 61 disease categories with 160 classes, covering both humans and animals. We built this with images from trusted public repositories, ensuring data diversity, quality, and ethical compliance. Additionally, we propose U ^2 -ViT, a novel diffusion-based text-to-image generation architecture arranging Vision Transformers (ViTs) in a nested U-Net structure to enhance the generation of diverse, and high-fidelity medical images. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that our model achieves the best Fr’echet Inception Distance (FID) score compared to state-of-the-art models. The source code is available at this https URL.

[CV-185] Accurate automated photo-identification of Near Eastern and European fire salamanders

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01601
作者: Maayan Yesharim,Hava Goldstein,Gabi Kolodny,Assaf Ben-Levy,Tamar Kis-Papo,Dor Gavish,Rotem Vidan,Nirit Lavie-Alon,Olga Rybak,Yoav Ram
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Quantitative Methods (q-bio.QM)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Photo-identification underpins non-invasive capture-recapture monitoring of amphibians, but manual identification becomes slow and error-prone as reference libraries grow. Focusing on the Near Eastern fire salamander (Salamandra infraimmaculata), we developed a pipeline based on zero-shot local-feature matching (SuperPoint and LightGlue) without species-specific training and evaluated it on 2,440 field photographs from Haifa and Tel Dan in northern Israel. We isolated the yellow spot pattern, scored image similarity by the number of high-confidence keypoint matches, which reduced a confound whereby many-spotted individuals accumulate spurious matches, and assigned identities across the database by two-tier clustering. Pipeline-assisted expert review corrected misidentifications, reducing the number of identities by almost a quarter. On held-out individuals, the pipeline ranked the correct individual first for 95.2% of queries and recovered identities with an ARI of 0.958 . Without modification, it reached 95.1% and 91.7% top-1 accuracy on two datasets of the European fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) and recognised 93.7% of recaptures in one of them, compared with 38 - 77% for five established programs and 93.9% for visual inspection. Zero-shot local-feature matching thus offers amphibian monitoring a re-identification tool that needs no training data, transfers between related species, scales to databases of over a thousand individuals, and can audit existing databases before capture-recapture analysis.

[CV-186] SCOUT: Planning under Occlusion via Object-Centric World Model Rollouts

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01600
作者: Amir Hossain Raj,Xuesu Xiao
类目: Robotics (cs.RO); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Robots manipulating in cluttered spaces must often plan from partial views where foreground objects occlude the target, surrounding geometry, and usable free space. Reactive policies often miss these hidden constraints, while exhaustive search becomes computationally prohibitive in dense clutter. We present SCOUT, an occlusion-aware planning framework that bridges high-level deliberation with grounded physical rollouts. SCOUT leverages an object-centric scene representation to reconstruct hidden geometry and derive a relational planning state capturing blocker hierarchies and accessibility corridors. To navigate the vast action space in clutter, an LLM proposes structured action candidates which are then rigorously evaluated via Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) using a learned action-conditioned world model. Evaluations on ‘Reveal’ and ‘Placement’ tasks show that SCOUT outperforms Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, embodied agents, and 3D world models, with significant gains in long-horizon tasks requiring reasoning over occluded geometry. We further validate the framework’s robustness through real-world robotic manipulation in a cluttered shelf environment.

[CV-187] Recoverability-Aware Evaluation of Diffusion Video Inpainting and Object Removal

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01578
作者: Yanliang Qi,Jiacheng Ding,Cong Guo,Peihua Mai
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 10 pages, 6 figures, 7 tables

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Video inpainting for object removal is scored over the whole hole, although the background behind the object is visible in other frames of the shot for some hole pixels and in no frame for others. A whole-hole score therefore mixes copying with generation and cannot show which of the two a remover does well. To separate the two, we propose recoverability-stratified evaluation, in which a point tracker run on the clean video labels each hole pixel by whether and how far away it is observed, so that fidelity and temporal stability can be reported per stratum against a copy reference. To reuse the observed content, we also propose evidence-guided sampling (EGS), which blends tracked colors into the clean-latent prediction of a video diffusion remover without training. On DAVIS, the perceptual advantage of three diffusion removers over flow propagation shrinks where the content is visible a few frames away (LPIPS difference-in-differences +0.046 to +0.056 against E2FGVI-HQ), and real paired captures show the same pattern for two of them. Their DAVIS hole warping error is two to four times that of ProPainter, and copying along clean-video tracks lowers their recoverable LPIPS by a quarter to two fifths. EGS closes 43% and 56% of the gap to this copy reference on held-out DAVIS when its colors come from clean-video tracks. With colors tracked on the masked input, a pre-registered confirmation finds no gain on MiniMax-Remover and a loss on ROSE. Diffusion removers thus leave observed content unused on DAVIS, and training-free reuse does not yet hold with tracked evidence.

[CV-188] Spend the Bits Where the Tiny Objects Are: Rate-Utility Region Coding for Aerial Detection

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01573
作者: Yanliang Qi,Jiacheng Ding,Cong Guo,Peihua Mai
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 17 pages, including supplementary material

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Bandwidth-limited aerial cameras must compress their images before a remote detector can find the many tiny objects in them. Threshold-based region-of-interest (ROI) coding sends only confidently detected regions, and because tiny objects provide limited visual evidence and often score low, it can discard the regions that contain them. We propose rate-utility region coding (RUO), which sends a region when its expected detection utility justifies its measured byte cost, choosing to drop it or to send it at low or high quality with one multiplier shared across images. RUO trains no model, uses a standard image codec and decodes in a few milliseconds. On all 1,610 VisDrone-DET test-dev images, RUO uses 42.4% fewer bits than a tuned threshold-based ROI coder, averaged over their shared tiny-object average precision (AP) range. RUO also needs fewer bits for tiny objects than the AV1 Image File Format (AVIF), High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) and three published learned codecs, and its advantage over threshold-based ROI coding persists when the sender and receiver use different detectors. For AP over all object sizes RUO needs 25.4% more bits than the tuned ROI coder, because its allocation drops large regions first at low rates, so it suits tasks that target tiny objects. We plan to release the code.

[CV-189] xt-Assisted Event Stream Visual Place Recognition via Multi-Scale Spatiotemporal Optimal Transport ICLR2027

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01558
作者: Lan Chen,Xingxing Xiong,Xiao Wang,Ziyan Zhang,Zikang Yan,Yuanhao Zheng,Bo Jiang,Yonghong Tian
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 17 pages including appendix, 4 figures. Submitted to ICLR 2027

Abstract:Benefiting from the high dynamic range, high temporal resolution, and low energy consumption of event cameras, low-altitude economic research leveraging event cameras has become a popular topic. Several existing attempts introduce natural-language descriptions into visual place recognition (VPR) to mitigate the sparsity of structural spatial information inherent to event cameras. Nevertheless, these methods still fail to fully address two core challenges: effectively encoding event streams and semantically aligning event streams with text. In this paper, we propose a multi-scale spatial-temporal optimal transport approach, MSTOT-EPR, to address these challenges. Specifically, given event streams and scene text information, we first adopt a visual encoder and a text encoder to extract respective feature representations. We then apply optimal-transport constraints to achieve cross-modal alignment. We then design a cross-modal bottleneck fusion module to further fuse bimodal features. Furthermore, we develop multi-scale spatial optimal transport and inter-frame temporal optimal transport modules to mine high-quality spatial-temporal event features for scene recognition. Extensive experiments on the NYC-Event-VPR and EPRBench datasets fully validate the effectiveness of our proposed framework for event-based VPR. The source code of this paper will be released upon acceptance.

[CV-190] opoDPO: Dense Preference Alignment for Structure-Sensitive Aerial Referring Segmentation

作者: Huaiyuan Peng,Jisheng Dang,Wencan Zhang,Jingwen Zhao,Hong Peng,Wenjun Ma,Bin Hu,Qi Tian,Tat-Seng Chua
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Abstract:Preference optimization for multimodal segmentation faces a granularity mismatch: dense masks contain spatially heterogeneous preference signals, whereas image-level objectives assign one shared nonlinear weight to all spatial margins. We introduce TopoDPO, a topology-aware dense preference alignment framework for structure-sensitive aerial referring segmentation. Topo-Prior mines informative preference pairs using connected-component discrepancy and macro-corner recall, while the dense objective applies the preference penalty to each local margin before spatial aggregation against a frozen supervised reference. On Topo-RS-Hard, a 4590-instance structural stress set, TopoDPO improves intersection over union (IoU) from 50.91% to 51.24% over image-level direct preference optimization (DPO) and reduces Betti-0 error from 1.34 to 0.90; paired image-cluster bootstrap intervals against image-level DPO exclude zero for all five reported metrics. Matched supervised controls and a complete factorial analysis separate the effects of topology-aware pair mining, localized correction, and dense reference-relative preference weighting. An unfiltered stratification over all 39,244 validation records further shows the clearest structural gains on samples with moderate or severe pre-alignment component-count errors. The code is publicly available at: this https URL.

[CV-191] Detecting Generated-Depth Injection Attacks on RGB-D Place Authentication

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01550
作者: Seigo Kawachi,Satoshi Matsuura
类目: Cryptography and Security (cs.CR); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 6 pages, 1 figure, 1 table. Accepted to IEEE WIFS 2026. © 2026 IEEE

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Advances in monocular depth estimation (MDE) now let an attacker generate depth from publicly available RGB images and submit forged RGB-D queries. Such attacks break a core assumption of RGB-D place authentication: that depth comes from a sensor. We study a presentation attack detection (PAD) classifier that uses geometric consistency between the enrollment and query views, as a software-layer defense. A three-stage evaluation shows how far this classifier detects software-injected depth, depending on how accurately the attacker knows the camera intrinsics. In the first stage, the attacker has only an estimate of the intrinsics, and the PAD classifier separates forgeries generated by all three MDE models with a validation area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.997-0.999. In the second stage, the attacker obtains the exact intrinsics, and the original PAD classifier falls to near chance (AUC 0.54-0.61); a retrained PAD classifier, however, still has the registration residual between enrollment and query as a cue. In the third stage, an oracle evaluation, in which the evaluator fits warps using the ground-truth 3D geometry, shows that detection falls to near chance only in its strongest case, where every valid query keypoint is given its ground-truth 3D coordinate. Of the detection cues, the reprojection error captures the attacker’s misestimate of the intrinsics, whereas the registration residual remains even when the attacker knows the exact intrinsics.

[CV-192] Band2Net: Frequency-to-Network Transport Distillation for fMRI-Privileged EEG-Only Session-Condition Decoding

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01548
作者: Nishi Kanta Paul,Md Shihabul Islam Shovo,Dwarikanath Mahapatra
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 5 pages, 2 figures, 1 table

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Functional MRI resolves large-scale brain networks but is expensive and stationary, whereas EEG is portable but poorly localised. We treat fMRI as privileged information, available during training and absent at deployment, with EEG and fMRI acquired from the same participants under matched conditions but not simultaneously. Band2Net encodes EEG into five frequency-specific connectivity graphs and fMRI into seven canonical network tokens from a frozen teacher, and solves a balanced entropic transport problem between the two token sets that gives each EEG band its own fMRI target. In subject-grouped cross-validation on the PsiConnect psilocybin data set, Band2Net reaches 0.801 ROC-AUC for EEG-only session-condition decoding, 5.0 AUC points (95% CI 1.8-8.2) above an EEG-only student. Although its margins over a single shared plan, a KL-relaxed plan and label-free network descriptors remain unresolved, secondary comparisons favour band-specific transported targets over logit, global-feature, contrastive and pooled-target distillation, though not after Holm correction.

[CV-193] GSExplorer: Interactive World Generation with a Persistent 3D Gaussian World State

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01543
作者: Sicheng Yu,Liu Liu,Xinjie Wang,Xinjiang Wang,Taojun Ding,Wenhao Hu,Beizhen Zhao,Puxin Yan,Zhizhong Su,Hao Wang
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)
备注: 17 pages

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Interactive world generation requires both accurate local control and stable scene consistency over long rollouts. Existing methods improve local generation through camera or geometry conditioning and extend historical context with memory mechanisms. However, long-horizon exploration remains challenging as target-view guidance becomes incomplete and inconsistencies accumulate across repeated scene updates. We present \textbfGSExplorer, a generation–reconstruction framework built around a persistent 3D Gaussian world state. At each step, the current 3DGS scene provides multimodal rendering conditions for a condition-driven video generator, while camera geometry is injected through a separate Relative Ray Encoding branch. Generated videos are then fed back to a SLAM-based reconstruction backend, where inconsistency filtering prevents conflicting content from corrupting the scene and cross-chunk bundle adjustment improves spatial alignment across generation steps. We further design a data-construction pipeline that reproduces realistic 3DGS degradation during scene extrapolation, yielding 293K training pairs of degraded multimodal renderings and real target videos. GSExplorer achieves the best overall performance among the compared methods on both single-step and three-step WorldScore evaluation, with strong camera control and consistency across both settings, including a Camera Control score of 99.07 in single-step extrapolation. On 481-frame leave-and-return rollouts, it also shows strong revisit consistency, demonstrating the value of maintaining a reliable 3D world state for continued exploration.

[CV-194] MoPort: A View-Aware 2D Interface for Motion Language Models

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01541
作者: Lixing Tan,Qing Xia,Yuting Guo,Shuai Li,Aimin Hao
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Motion language models (MoLMs) encode 3D human motion as discrete tokens for language-based understanding. Deploying them on monocular video raises two problems. Pose detection yields 2D joint sequences, leaving a dimensional gap from the 3D motion used in training. Moreover, the 2D observation changes with the camera viewpoint, while the depth lost in projection makes the 2D pose ambiguous across viewpoints. We propose MoPort, a view-aware 2D interface that enables MoLMs to take 2D observations as input. We introduce Paired View Alignment (PVA), which gives two views of the same motion a shared 3D teacher target and directly constrains the consistency of their latents, so that 2D observations from different viewpoints are mapped to a consistent semantic representation. Camera-Modulated Encoding (CME) estimates the camera extrinsics from the 2D sequence and uses them to modulate encoding, providing the 2D latents with geometric information about the viewpoint. MoPort achieves R@1 of 0.5674 on HumanML3D and 0.3286 on KIT-ML, outperforming all evaluated baselines. On HumanML3D, its R@1 decreases only from 0.5763 on in-distribution viewpoints to 0.5585 on out-of-distribution viewpoints. We validate portability on three downstream MoLMs. Furthermore, on the real-world RGB video dataset Fit3D, MoPort achieves 80.36% accuracy. Code will be released upon acceptance.

[CV-195] CUFormer: Modality-Aware CT-Ultrasound Point Cloud Registration for Orthopedic Navigation

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01536
作者: Lixing Tan,Qing Xia,Yuting Guo,Shuai Li,Aimin Hao
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Registering intraoperative Ultrasound (US) bone-surface point clouds to preoperative Computed Tomography (CT) models can support radiation-free orthopedic navigation. Differences in imaging physics produce distinct surface sampling patterns, complicating cross-modal feature matching. Bone strongly reflects ultrasound and casts an acoustic shadow, so US captures only the probe-facing bone surface and leaves most CT points unmatched. This partial coverage makes correspondences ambiguous on near-symmetric bones. We propose CUFormer, a modality-aware registration framework. We introduce a Modality-Aware Transformer (MAT) that encodes input modality through identity embeddings and updates features through modality-specific adapters within a shared geometric matcher. We model imaging visibility and use predicted reference-side visibility to weight coarse and fine correspondences. CUFormer achieves the lowest mean registration errors among evaluated methods on two CT-US datasets, UltraBones100k and UltraBonesHip, and the CT-RGB-D dataset SpineDepth. On UltraBones100k, it reaches mean rotation error 4.53 ^\circ , translation error 3.19,mm, and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) 2.54,mm, reducing RMSE by 65.8% relative to the best-performing baseline by this metric. These results demonstrate CUFormer’s effectiveness in aligning partial bone surfaces with preoperative CT across anatomical sites.

[CV-196] AbacusGS: Gaussian Splatting without Per-Splat Sorting

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01534
作者: Jiacheng Ding,Yanliang Qi,Cong Guo,Peihua Mai
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Graphics (cs.GR)
备注: 10 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables

点击查看摘要

Abstract:3D Gaussian Splatting sorts every splat by depth in every frame. Viewers that draw splats with the hardware rasterizer and sort them on the CPU, as most web and mobile viewers do, spend most of the frame time in this sort. We present AbacusGS, which stores the blending order of a 3DGS scene in the scene layout. AbacusGS groups the splats into octree boxes of at most 128 splats and stores each box in order along an axis chosen at write time. In each frame, AbacusGS sorts only the visible boxes, and one dot product per box decides whether the box is read forward or backward. A short order-aware fine-tuning converts an existing 3DGS model, and the over operator of 3DGS stays unchanged. On 13 standard scenes, AbacusGS loses 0.13 dB PSNR on average against an equally fine-tuned 3DGS model. In an OpenGL viewer that orders splats on the CPU, AbacusGS renders frames 4.5 times faster than per-splat sorting. We also present a compact format of 17 bytes per splat and a CUDA tile renderer that use the same order. The code will be released.

[CV-197] AR-RRG: Anatomy-Guided Retrieval-Driven Radiology Report Generation

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01529
作者: Xiang Zhang,Shijie Song,Wanqing Zhao,Wei Zhou,Rui Cao,Dekui Wang,Qiyao Hu,Xianlin Peng,Hangzai Luo,Sheng Zhong,Jianping Fan
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Radiology report generation (RRG) streamlines clinical workflows and alleviates the burden of radiologists’ documentation. Standard vision-language models capture global visual cues and lack fine-grained alignment between anatomical regions and diagnostic text. Most retrieval-augmented methods retrieve complete historical reports, introducing redundant noise and severe vision-text mismatches that trigger clinically risky hallucinations and missed lesions. In this paper, we introduce AR-RRG, an anatomy-guided retrieval-driven method for the generation of radiology reports. AR-RRG consists of two core modules: the anatomy-aware self-training lesion detection network (ASLDNet) and the retrieval-driven radiology report generation (RRRG). ASLDNet leverages anatomy-aware spatial verification (ASV) and class-adaptive dynamic thresholding (CDT) via self-training, delivering accurate lesion localization to support subsequent generation. As the generative branch of AR-RRG, RRRG eliminates clinical hallucinations through dual-granularity retrieval (DR) and complements missing lesions with a neighborhood consensus (NC) mechanism. A parallel continuous visual perception (PCVP) stream converts radiographs into visual tokens through fixed medical encoding and resampling. Multi-scale text and visual features are fused, followed by LoRA-efficient large language model tuning to generate clinically consistent, visually grounded radiology reports. Extensive evaluations on MS-CXR, MIMIC-CXR, and IU X-Ray demonstrate that AR-RRG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across mainstream metrics. Our code will be made publicly available.

[CV-198] Label-Free Localization and Test-Time Suppression of CLIPs Typographic Circuits

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01513
作者: Bohan Liu,Wenqian Ye,Guangzhi Xiong,Zhenghao He,Sanchit Sinha,Aidong Zhang
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:CLIP-based Vision-Language Models have become cornerstones of modern multimodal systems. The cross-modal contrastive objective equips the CLIP vision encoder to both see objects and read text. These two abilities induce an entanglement between the encoding of lexical and semantic shapes, creating a distinctive vulnerability to typographic attacks, in which rendered text overrides an image’s semantic content with its literal meaning. The black-box nature of these encoders has prevented a mechanistic interpretation of such entanglement. We introduce a head-decomposed Sparse Dictionary Learning (SDL) architecture that, by design, decomposes individual attention heads into interpretable, head-specific latents. Based on this inductive disentanglement, we re-purpose Clarity Score and propose normalized Text Attribution Score, which are both label-free, to identify attention heads that carry typographic information. As a causal validation of successful circuit separation, we perform a mechanistic intervention that reweighs attention away from the patch tokens in the identified lexical heads at test-time. Experiments show that the intervention effectively recovers object classification under typographic attack and, across five CLIP variants and four typographic benchmarks, achieves up to 46.9% improvement while incurring up to 1% accuracy loss in general image perception, outperforming prior supervised and training-free methods. Expanding on the mechanistic intervention, we propose a test-time adaptive attention head routing to further reduce the impact on performance at matched robustness, pushing beyond the Pareto frontier of current robustness-perception tradeoff.

[CV-199] Resolve Clear or Defer: Training-Free Active Prototype Triage for Ecological Detection Pipelines WACV2027

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01466
作者: Anirudh Potlapally,Brijesh Nanda Brunda Yogananda,Jianyang Gu,Maanav Jajodia,Luke Meyers,Wei-Lun Chao,Hari Subramoni
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: Accepted to the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV 2027), Main Conference. 27 pages including supplementary material

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Ecological monitoring increasingly relies on camera traps and aerial surveys that generate large image collections. High-recall animal detectors can localize candidate animals at scale. However, they also produce many detections that still require expert review, including false positives, ambiguous cases, and animals difficult to identify at the species level. Since exhaustive review requires substantial effort, we propose training-free active prototype triage, where reviewed detections become reusable evidence to (1) Resolve supported foreground classes, (2) Clear likely background false positives, or (3) Defer insufficiently supported cases for expert review. Across camera-trap and aerial datasets, foreground recognition and false-positive rejection benefit from different pretrained representations: BioCLIP2 provides foreground evidence while DINOv3 provides background evidence, reducing erroneous foreground clearing while improving automatic foreground recovery. Deferring unsupported cases avoids the higher error rates caused by forced decisions. Compared with confidence-thresholded multiclass k-NN and uncertainty-sampling logistic regression, prototype triage improves foreground recovery while maintaining competitive or lower review burden. Acquisition goes beyond class discovery: even after classes are represented, prototype choice determines how reliably evidence propagates through the remaining detections. Our results suggest that once animal localization reaches high recall, the challenge shifts from finding animals to deciding which examples to review, how to reuse them, and when evidence does not support an automatic decision.

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01463
作者: Saarth Deshpande,Neeraja J. Yadwadkar,Venkat Arun

Abstract:Resource managers typically encode what to do in a task-specific policy—a heuristic, an optimization procedure, or a model trained for the task—that must be developed before use and may need revision as the workload or system changes. We propose bypassing policy development and instead asking pretrained models to make resource-management decisions directly, given the current system state, desired outcome, and available choices. We evaluate this approach on microservice autoscaling, DRAM sizing, and video encoding, using a frontier LLM and two small decision models. On two microservice applications, a small decision model meets latency targets while using within 10% of the replicas allocated by policy-based autoscalers and within 13% of the frontier LLM. In DRAM sizing, a small decision model reduces DRAM usage by up to 27.5% relative to static provisioning while maintaining at least 95% of baseline performance. In video encoding, it completes encodes up to 4.3 \times faster than the frontier LLM, with an imperceptible 1.1-point decrease in Video Multi-Method Assessment Fusion (VMAF), a metric of perceptual video quality. Making individual resource-management decisions may be considerably simpler than developing a general strategy for making them.

Abstract:Localized false-merge correction in connectomics requires converting an identified error into an executable native 3D partition. Abstract:Processing every video frame through Vision-Language Models (VLMs) adds significant inference cost and limits their ability to comprehend real-time video. Existing approaches either sub-sample frames uniformly, ignoring content and missing important events, or prune visual tokens inside the VLM to cut per-call cost while still invoking the model on every sampled frame. We introduce FOCUS, a training-free three-layer framework that reduces the number of invocations and steers each one towards what matters. Temporal gating measures inter-frame dissimilarity in the patch-embedding space of a smaller VLM from the same family, triggering burst captures only when the scene changes in a semantically meaningful way. Patch-level dissimilarity is then accumulated across the burst and fused with a top-down attention prior into a spatial focus map that encodes where motion and semantic relevance coincide. That map calibrates the VLM’s value cache during generation, progressively amplifying vision tokens in task-relevant regions and attenuating off-target ones, without removing any token from the context. The loop closes after each response: text-to-vision cross-attention is extracted from the decoder and fed back as the prior for the next burst, letting the system converge on semantically important regions over successive observations. Abstract:Human pose estimation under adverse lighting and occlusion conditions remains challenging for camera- and LiDAR-based systems. Unlike specialized radars, RadPose leverages monostatic full-duplex operation to extract channel impulse responses (CIRs) directly from standard OFDM communication signals, generating 3D radio point clouds without additional sensing hardware. It further adopts a joint-aware inverse kinematics refinement module based on graph convolution to enforce skeletal topology, bone-length consistency, and anatomical plausibility. Abstract:Spectral imagery, including hyperspectral image (HSI) and multispectral image (MSI), exhibits substantial heterogeneity in band numbers, wavelengths, spectral resolutions, hindering unified modeling and cross-sensor transfer. From the perspective of imaging physics, these heterogeneous observations can be regarded as discrete measurements of an underlying continuous spectrum acquired through different sampling processes. Motivated by this perspective, we propose SpecUltra, a unified foundation model for heterogeneous spectral images. Specifically, SpecUltra employs 3D convolutional tokenization and wavelength-aware 3D RoPE to encode relative wavelength and spatial relationships, enabling fine-grained spatial-spectral modeling within a shared coordinate system. We further construct MultiHyper-200K, a large-scale multi-sensor HSI dataset, and pretrain SpecUltra using auxiliary-token-assisted mask image modeling (MIM), where a level token indicates the radiometric product type and register tokens absorb sensor- and acquisition-dependent variations. To bridge the spectral-granularity gap between HSI and MSI, we introduce Spectral Kernel Transformation (SKT), which transfers pretrained knowledge in parameter space by constructing MSI embedding kernels from fine-grained HSI-pretrained kernel slices. This design preserves pretrained spectral priors while maintaining compatibility with the pretrained backbone. Experiments on HSI and MSI classification and segmentation benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art or competitive performance across disparate sensors and downstream tasks.

Abstract:Optimizing vision models for accuracy does not force the model to learn and utilize human-understandable and domain-specific concepts and rules. We propose explaining image classifications through domain-specific concepts, visual evidence, and expert knowledge expressed as logical rules. We introduce FLUENT (Framework for Localized, Uncertainty-Aware Explanations in Normative Terminology), a post-hoc framework that ranks expert-authored rules combining jointly required, alternative, and absent concepts. To account for prediction errors, FLUENT combines predicted labels and concept states with empirically estimated likelihoods and concept priors. It scores each rule by calculating support over satisfying assignments to the concepts mentioned in that rule, then normalizes these scores to express relative confidence among candidate explanations. The selected rule is illustrated through occlusion-based highlights for positive concept mentions in the query image and localized examples in retrieved reference images for negative mentions. These illustrations are intended to show end users unfamiliar with the domain what the concepts named in an explanation look like. FLUENT combines domain knowledge and model accuracy, and delivers visual concept highlights and explicit rule confidence to explain an image in the vocabulary of an application domain.

Abstract:Visually realistic video generation does not guarantee physically consistent motion. Generated objects may exhibit implausible collision responses or rebounds without energy dissipation, while even physically valid motion predictions may not be faithfully realized during synthesis. We propose \textbfIMPACT, a physics-state-driven image-to-video framework that addresses these challenges by coupling explicit dynamics prediction with complementary sparse–dense physical guidance. A learnably calibrated Physics State Generator unifies continuous free-flight dynamics with discrete collision responses, linking impact timing, post-impact velocity, rebound attenuation, and eventual settling within a coherent physical-state sequence. To translate this evolution into effective generative constraints, IMPACT derives sparse trajectories and dense region-level motion priors from the same physical rollout. Sparse trajectories constrain global object displacement, while dense priors guide diffusion sampling to encourage coherent object-region motion and suppress unwanted background changes. Their shared physical basis coordinates global and local motion guidance to reduce prediction–generation mismatch. Experiments on 100 controlled sphere–plane collision scenes spanning different material combinations and visual environments demonstrate improved physical plausibility over representative general-purpose, physics-grounded, and motion-controllable baselines. Abstract:We examine the main claims of Zada, Benou, and Irani (2021), which states that in an image classification task with imbalanced training data, (i) using pure noise to augment minority-class images encourages generalization by improving minority-class accuracy. This method is paired with (ii) a new batch normalization layer that normalizes noise images using affine parameters learned from natural images, which improves the model’s performance. Moreover, (iii) this improvement is robust to varying levels of data augmentation. Finally, the authors propose that (iv) adding pure noise images can improve classification even on balanced training data. We implemented the training pipeline from the description of the paper using PyTorch and integrated authors’ code snippets for sampling pure noise images and batch normalizing noise and natural images separately. We reproduced the main claims that (i) oversampling with pure noise improves generalization by improving the minority-class accuracy, (ii) the proposed batch normalization (BN) method outperforms baselines, (iii) and this improvement is robust across data augmentations. Our results also support that (iv) adding pure noise images can improve classification on balanced training data. However, additional experiments suggest that the performance improvement from OPeN may be more orthogonal to the improvement caused by a bigger network or more complex data augmentation.

作者: Ziming Liu,Yizhan Qu,Leichen Wang,Hao Sun
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Robotics (cs.RO)

Abstract:End-to-end planners decode the ego trajectory either by coordinate regression, which is fast but blends plausible maneuvers into one trajectory that may follow none of them, or by diffusion and flow matching, which model the trajectory distribution but need several inference steps. Drifting models move this iteration into training: a one-step generator learns to follow an attraction–repulsion field between generated and ground-truth samples. Drifting was developed for class-conditional image generation, where every class supplies many positive samples. In planning, every scene is its own condition. Pooling scenes would attract the generated trajectories of one scene to the ground truth of unrelated scenes, whereas computing the field per scene leaves a single positive, the expert trajectory. Mutual repulsion then holds the generated trajectories on a shell around it, so any single generated trajectory deviates from the ground truth. We present DriftingPlanner, a trajectory planner trained with the drifting loss alone, without any coordinate regression term. It computes the field per scene and removes the shell at inference: it decodes every noise vector together with its negation in one batched pass, and averaging each antithetic pair cancels the linear part of the displacement from the shell center. On NAVSIM navtest, DriftingPlanner reaches a state-of-the-art 93.75 PDMS, and with single-step inference its drifting decoder comes within 0.13 PDMS of the best diffusion or flow matching setting, which needs ten inference steps.

Abstract:Streaming video question answering (QA) requires real-time reasoning over continuous video streams under strict latency and active-context budgets. Current streaming vision-language models (VLMs) often give confident yet ungrounded answers when queries are ambiguous or have false premises, or when relevant visual evidence is no longer in the active context. Proactive clarification can help, but must satisfy the same latency and memory constraints. We present StreamClarify, a training-free framework for grounded streaming QA that combines a pre-answer uncertainty check with hierarchical memory. The check uses the entropy of a binary pre-answer judgment as a lightweight uncertainty score to decide whether to answer directly or request clarification. We further construct StreamClarify-QA, a diagnostic benchmark of 1,837 QA pairs from StreamBench and OVO-Bench, spanning standard, referential ambiguity, and unanswerable scenarios. Across three VLM backbones, StreamClarify improves Macro accuracy by up to 8.2 points over backbone-matched baselines. At comparable trigger rates, entropy-based selection achieves more than 18 points higher precision than random selection in identifying initially incorrect answers. We also report a controlled, oracle-assisted Qwen3-VL simulation on Ambiguous QA with generated questions and referent-only user replies, where the entropy-gated condition improves accuracy by 8.3 points.

Abstract:Large vision-language models (LVLMs) routinely use inference-time visual-token compression to prune hundreds of patch tokens down to a compact budget. Existing LVLM backdoors fire whenever a triggered image appears, whereas prior deployment-triggered attacks activate only when model weights are quantized or pruned. However, conventional LVLM backdoors exhibit nearly 100% attack success rate (ASR) under full-token inference, immediately exposing compromised checkpoints during pre-deployment auditing. We reveal context stripping: surrounding clean visual tokens suppress an embedded trigger at full length, whereas token pruning strips this context away and activates the backdoor. Motivated by this finding, we propose StripWake, a projector-only backdoor that remains dormant under full-token auditing yet activates across unseen compressors. Specifically, StripWake pairs clean-supervised full-token views with target-supervised randomized compressed views, and aligns early visual attention with a frozen benign teacher to preserve clean utility. On LLaVA-1.5-7B across nine unseen compressors, StripWake stays dormant at 0.4% full-token ASR yet achieves 94.0%-99.7% compressed ASR across five primary compressors without CIDEr loss.

Abstract:We reproduce the central claims of INP-Former, a reconstruction-based method for multi-class industrial anomaly detection. INP-Former extracts Intrinsic Normal Prototypes (INPs) from each test image and uses them to guide a decoder that reconstructs normal features, without a stored memory bank. Using the authors’ released code, we reproduce the reported performance on MVTec AD and VisA and extend the evaluation to MVTec AD 2, where image AUROC with the default settings is 63.4, compared with 99.7 on MVTec AD. On MVTec AD, a five-seed ablation shows that most of the performance comes from the INP mechanism, while the two auxiliary losses add small changes whose direction depends on the metric. A paired comparison with both losses disabled confirms the benefit of INP on MVTec AD 2. The default of six prototypes transfers less well: the plateau beyond four prototypes reproduces on MVTec AD and VisA, but on MVTec AD 2 a single prototype outperforms six in AU-PRO on the public split and on both hidden test splits. 作者: Merle Diedrichsen,Koen Van Leemput,Douglas N. Greve,Oula Puonti,Axel Thielscher

Abstract:Personalized computational head models for biophysical simulations rely on accurate whole-head segmentations from T1-weighted (T1w) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans. While T1w scans provide excellent contrast for intracranial anatomy, extracerebral tissues have partly almost no signal (compact bone) and also suffer from the so-called chemical shift artifact, which affects the fatty tissues in MRI and causes them to spatially shift in the frequency encoding direction of the scan. This artifact occurs primarily in two structures of the head: the spongy bone, a fatty compartment inside the compact bone, and the subcutaneous fat, located directly underneath the skin. The frequency-encoding direction is often set in the superior-inferior direction, causing the fatty tissues to shift down and, as a result, making the skull appear thinner than it actually is. Existing segmentation methods do not model this artifact, consequently leading to inaccurate labeling of the skull and scalp, which introduces a bias in biophysical simulations. The direction and magnitude of the fat-shift can be determined from the scan parameters, thus making it possible to explicitly model the shift and to recover the correct anatomy. This study introduces a probabilistic model that uses variational inference to segment head and brain structures from a T1w scan while accounting for the fat-shift artifact. The proposed Fat-shift-informed Label Optimization of the Whole head (FLOW) method reconstructs extracerebral anatomy more accurately than a fat-shift-agnostic segmentation approach while maintaining high segmentation accuracy in all other structures. FLOW-based fat-shift corrected segmentations significantly reduce bias in electric field simulations compared to a segmentation method that does not model the shift.

Abstract:Diffusion-based vision-language-action (VLA) models cascade pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) with diffusion action experts, but typically restrict the VLM to providing static conditioning. This separation limits how much pretrained perception and reasoning can guide action generation, especially in out-of-distribution settings. We introduce JADE, a Joint Action DEnoiser that enables the VLM and action expert to jointly refine actions. Our key insight is that structured action latents allow the VLM to read the current noisy action together with visual observations and language instructions. At every denoising step, the VLM contextualizes the noisy action and guides the action expert through gated cross-attention, so that its guidance evolves with the action being generated. We further supervise the VLM to recover clean action latents from noisy ones, which gives it a direct action-learning signal and couples perception with control. Additionally, joint denoising enables JADE to generate actions with fewer sampling steps, helping offset the additional cost of VLM participation. An adaptive step-size schedule further balances task performance and inference latency. On RoboDojo, JADE achieves an average success rate of 12.67%, the highest among the evaluated \pi_0.5 -based methods, and is competitive with recent VLA and WAM foundation models pretrained at scale. Abstract:4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) models are computationally expensive to train but distributed as easily copied parameter files. Existing watermarks protect these assets by fine-tuning the scene against a neural decoder to extract bit strings from rendered video, a heavy process vulnerable to the temporal dynamics of dynamic scenes. However, if the threat model targets the redistributed file itself, verification can be vastly simplified. Because the canonical Spherical-Harmonic (SH) coefficients of 4DGS are time- and view-invariant, parameter-space perturbations can be recovered via deterministic arithmetic. We propose SHield, the first non-blind, decoder-free watermarking approach that natively embeds full-resolution RGB images into 4DGS files. SHield tiles a zero-mean payload across the SH coefficients of a key-selected Gaussian subset, applying a brief anchored optimization to preserve visual fidelity. To verify ownership, it geometrically re-associates the key using canonical Gaussian centres to survive file tampering and recovers the payload in closed form. Across 30 scenes (D-NeRF, HyperNeRF, DyNeRF), SHield guarantees near-perfect payload recovery (Pearson r \geq 0.991 ) on all 150 tested models with a mean rendering penalty of \leq 0.13 ~dB. Held-out evaluation yields perfect detection on 400 true trials and zero false positives across 1,600 wrong-subset null trials. We also strictly bound the method’s robustness: SHield survives INT8 quantization and 30% opacity pruning for the image payload, and on aggressive SH-degree-1 truncation bit payloads are still decodable.

Abstract:Spatial transcriptomics measures gene expression while preserving where each cell sits in the tissue. Beyond improved image quality, GESTALT natively synthesizes at 1024 x 1024, and is evaluated in three generalization settings: zero-shot transfer across gene panels and datasets, held-out patients and disease states, and transfer across studies and tissue sources. Abstract:Streaming video LLMs can now commentate live gameplay, but they are trained and tested on the same games. We propose StreamDuo, which pairs a trainable commentator with a frozen research agent that reads the wiki of the game being played. When the commentator sees something it cannot name, it sends the current frames, and the research agent returns a few wiki entries two seconds later while the stream continues. Abstract:Many Automated Speaker Verification Systems (ASVs) commonly employ liveliness detection techniques, such as VoicePop, which identify genuine speech by analyzing low- frequency pop bursts from plosive phonemes using Gammatone Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (GFCC) and an SVM classifier. Abstract:3D visual grounding localizes objects in 3D scenes from natural language descriptions, requiring reasoning over semantics, spatial relationships, and multi-view observations. Abstract:Persistent homology (PH) is a mathematically principled multi-scale topological descriptor of shape and connectivity in data. It is widely applied in image classification, segmentation, and shape analysis across medical and aerial imaging, providing structural information that pixel-wise deep learning may overlook. Standard cubical PH decomposes an image into cubical cells (vertices, edges, and squares) and reduces them sequentially in filtration order. This sequential reduction has \Theta(n) parallel depth for an n -pixel image, limiting within-image GPU parallelism and constraining its use in topology-aware deep learning. We introduce CuPH, a GPU-based parallel algorithm for computing cubical PH on 2D images that operates directly on pixels rather than cubical cells. CuPH buckets pixels by filtration values, activates them with a level-synchronous sweep, and tracks connected components with a lock-free union-find method. We prove that CuPH produces persistence diagrams identical to standard cubical PH on integer inputs, with a stability bound for floating-point inputs. CuPH reduces parallel depth from \Theta(n) to O(L\log n) for an image with L intensity levels. We implement the level sweep as a single CUDA kernel, eliminating cross-level kernel-launch overhead. Empirically, CuPH is 18.6 – 99.6\times faster than the existing GPU baseline (CMP). As a drop-in PH backend, CuPH accelerates topology-aware classification ( 4.2 – 16.7\times ) and segmentation ( 8.3 – 44\times ) while preserving accuracy. It also enables computing full-image PH losses on high-resolution images, improving segmentation Dice by 2.2 – 4.6 points over patch-local PH baselines and accelerating training by 25 – 31\times .

Abstract:Cross-view object geo-localization (CVOGL) aims to localize a target in a satellite image from an observation captured under another viewpoint. Existing methods typically specify the query with a click point or bounding box, marking the target region but underusing the semantic attributes and relations conveyed by natural language. Moreover, referring expressions are often viewpoint-dependent, making query-view descriptions difficult to ground directly in the satellite image. In this paper, we formulate cross-view visual grounding (CVVG), extending conventional point- or box-prompted CVOGL to instance grounding jointly guided by a referring expression and a visual exemplar. We present GAV (Grounding Across Views), a view-aware framework for selectively transferring visual and linguistic evidence across views. Its core is view-aware referring reasoning: target-centered descriptions are derived from the marked query image, checked for target-category consistency, and augmented with a direction-free role cue. Exemplar prompting, cross-view alignment, and scene-level discrimination ground this semantic evidence in a satellite instance. GAV achieves a new state of the art on MoP-UAV with 62.55% Acc@0.5. We also introduce CVOGL-Text, a benchmark for text-guided grounding from street- and drone-view queries to satellite images. GAV outperforms the click-point baseline by 7.09 and 6.79 Acc@0.25 points on the street- and drone-view splits, respectively, demonstrating robustness to larger viewpoint gaps. The code and annotations will be publicly released.

[CV-221] Robust Pixel-wise Digital Image Correlation under Large Motions and Illumination Variations via a Global-to-Local Hybrid Neural Field

作者: Xianglong Guo,Jianyang Li
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Machine Learning (cs.LG)
备注: 28 pages, 12 figures, 4 tables

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Digital image correlation (DIC) is a widely used non-contact technique for full-field displacement measurement. Data-driven deep-learning DIC offers rapid inference but may generalize poorly to unseen speckle patterns, deformation modes, noise levels, and illumination conditions. Classical optimization-based DIC and recent image-constrained neural formulations avoid labeled displacement data, yet their convergence and accuracy remain vulnerable to initialization, large rigid-body motion, fine non-uniform deformation, and gray-value disturbances. This paper presents a global-to-local hybrid neural DIC framework for robust pixelwise measurement. Stage 1 estimates a dominant in-plane rigid transformation through coarse rotation search, phase correlation, and masked refinement, providing a reliable initialization under large translation and rotation. Stage 2 represents the residual displacement with a hybrid Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN) and multilayer perceptron (MLP), and optimizes it using a valid-overlap, illumination-robust structural loss. The local gray-value model explicitly accommodates multiplicative and additive intensity changes. Simulated and real experiments demonstrate accurate and stable displacement recovery under noise, non-uniform deformation, large rotation, illumination variation, and degraded imaging conditions.

[CV-222] Efficient Image Denoising on Smartphone GPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report

Abstract:Image denoising is a fundamental problem in mobile photography. Despite a large number of solutions proposed for this task, the majority of them are trained on synthetically produced noisy images, and are additionally too computationally heavy for processing full-resolution images on mobile devices. This creates a need for efficient deep learning-based models that are not only performant but can also be deployed on constrained mobile hardware. In this Mobile AI challenge, we address this problem and propose the participants to design fast solutions that can denoise Full HD resolution photos while running on popular smartphone GPUs from Qualcomm and Arm. For this, the participants were provided with a large-scale dataset consisting of noisy-clean image pairs captured in the wild. The runtime of all models was evaluated on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and Dimensity 9500 chipsets with the Adreno and Mali GPUs, respectively. Top solutions proposed in this challenge are able to perform high-quality image denoising under 100 milliseconds on both platforms while reaching a PSNR score of over 37 dB. A comprehensive description of the models developed in the challenge is provided in this paper.

Abstract:Image super-resolution is widely used on mobile devices for upscaling various types of image data. This creates a need for efficient deep learning-based models that are not only performant but can also be deployed on neural processing units (NPUs) present in the majority of mobile and IoT chipsets. In this Mobile AI challenge, we address this problem and propose the participants to design fast solutions that can upsample images from Full HD to 4K resolution while running on popular mobile NPUs from Qualcomm and MediaTek. For this, the participants were provided with the DIV2K dataset and trained models to do an efficient 3X image upscaling. The competition had two tracks: in the first track, the models had to be fully quantized (INT8), and the runtime of all models was evaluated on the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 NPU. In the second track, the participants were developing floating-point solutions that were evaluated on the MediaTek Dimensity 9500 NPU. Top solutions proposed in this challenge are able to reconstruct 4K images under 5 milliseconds while reaching a PSNR score of 30 dB. A comprehensive description of the models developed in the challenge is provided in this paper.

[CV-224] PSF-Informed Reconstruction: An Enhanced 2D Directional Filtered Backprojection Method for Cone-Beam Rotary Computed Laminography

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00953
作者: Chengxiang Wang,Wei Yu,Baodong Liu
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Cone-beam rotary computed laminography (CL) presents a viable alternative to cone-beam CT for imaging objects with high aspect ratios. Conventional reconstruction techniques, such as CL-FBP and CL-FDK, often yield suboptimal results charac?terized by pronounced superimposition artifacts, reduced contrast,and blurred edges, primarily due to their reliance on 1D row-wise filtering along detector rows. To address these limitations and improve reconstruction quality, we proposed a novel 2D directional filtered backprojection (DFBP) method based on the point spread function (PSF). First, an exact expression for the projection process is derived by establishing the relationship between a reconstructed pixel and its corresponding projection point on the detector. Second, a revised backprojection process incorporating two weighting factors is introduced to counteract the nonlinearity inherent in conventional backprojection, leading to a simplified PSF formulation. Third, to circumvent the computational burden of 3D image space filtering,an approximate method by linearizing the coordinate relationship in Fourier space under some assumptions is developed that transfers the 3D filtering operation to the 2D projection space. This approach facilitates the derivation of a formally simple yet effective 2D direc?tional filter, which integrates a 2D von Hann window and a 2D sinc window. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method produces reconstructions with superior contrast, sharper boundaries,and fewer superimposition artifacts compared to CL-FBP and CL?FDK. Moreover, it enables more accurate recovery of internal structures, such as bubble defects and electronic components.

[CV-225] What Helps Denoising Can Hurt Memory: Rethinking History in Long Video Generation

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00937
作者: Yubin Jing,Ziyang Zhang,Meng Chen,Yuyao Li,Haofan Wang,Yichen Gong
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 41 pages, 9 figures, 56 tables

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Autoregressive video generators produce long videos block by block, using historical context to maintain temporal consistency. After denoising, a committing pass encodes each clean block into keys and values (KV) that later blocks read, and the same clean block can be encoded into different KV depending on the history it reads. We therefore study historical context not only as a condition for denoising but also as an input to committing. Older historical context that supports denoising can harm subsequent generation when read during committing. At fixed context size and temporal positions, older historical context lowers mean clip-to-clip Subject Consistency. Across 5 generator configurations supporting longer contexts, consistency rises, plateaus, and then declines as committing context expands. Motivated by these findings, we propose Commit Forcing, a training-free rule that organizes committing into a chain. During committing, each block reads only the preceding block’s stored KV, so older historical context reaches new entries only through the chain. We apply this rule to 6 pretrained generators. On 60-second VBench, Commit Forcing improves Quality and Total on all 6 generators, by up to 1.27 Quality points and 1.10 Total points. Long-range consistency gains extend to 240-second videos. In a blinded comparison on 120-second LongLive videos, Commit Forcing achieves win rates of 83.5% for subject and scene consistency and 82.9% for overall preference against the base generator, excluding ties.

[CV-226] ZOPGA-KD: Zeroth Order PGA Guided Data Free Knowledge Distillation

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00908
作者: Tuhin Subhra Mukherjee,Tiya Rose Pulikunnel,Vaidhav Adit,Devanand Thanissery,S.H. Shabbeer Basha
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Knowledge distillation (KD) enables the transfer of learned representations from a large teacher network to a small student network. In foundational KD, the student network uses the original training data of the teacher model to accomplish this task. However, due to privacy concerns, the original training data is often not available. To overcome this reliance on original training data, several data-free knowledge distillation methods have been developed. Some of these methods operate in the white-box setting, and a few methods generate synthetic data by training a generator network. White-box methods use the teacher model’s parameters to obtain a synthetic dataset. To avoid relying on teacher parameters, some methods use computationally expensive generative approaches to obtain such a dataset. There also exist certain black-box methods that generate the synthetic data without accessing teacher parameters. These methods are also computationally intensive. We propose a data-free knowledge distillation method that utilizes just the teacher’s output logits and does not require access to its architecture, parameters, or gradients. We generate synthetic data via Projected Gradient Ascent (PGA) starting from smooth random noise signals. Required gradients are obtained through zeroth-order gradient estimation rather than backpropagating through the teacher’s parameters. The student is then trained on these synthetically generated samples. We evaluate the proposed method on several benchmark datasets and show that the distillation performance is comparable with approaches that have access to the teacher model parameters.

[CV-227] FilmTogether: Cinematic Video Generation from Low-Cost Inputs

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00899
作者: Shiying Zhang,Xiaobin Hu,Qianchi Zhang,Jiaqi Zhao,Xiaoda Yang,Bo Yin,Shuicheng Yan
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 14 pages. Project page: this https URL

点击查看摘要

Abstract:The widespread adoption of mobile devices has democratized video recording, but a stark aesthetic divide persists between casual, low-cost captures and high-cost cinematic productions. Bridging this gap requires upgrading heterogeneous production elements, such as lighting, specialized costumes, and materials, without altering the core layout, identity, and temporal motion of the original footage. However, this task is heavily bottlenecked by two important challenges: 1) Lacking a high-quality paired training data specifically designed to handle complex low-to-high appearance shifts. 2) Ignoring the capacity of current video editing models to perceive and enhance the multiple low-cost compositions. To address these issues, we present CineCraft-120K, a large-scale dataset of aligned low- and high-cost video pairs annotated with pair-aware editing prompts. CineCraft-120K features a diverse, high-resolution and high-cost Cinematic Crafting bank spanning decades of media production, meticulously taxonomized into 5 broad domains and 23 fine-grained sub-categories. It also provides element-level mapping between low- and high-cost counterparts, offering pair-aware rich textual prompts that precisely detail the required aesthetic transformations while anchoring structural layout. Architecturally, we propose a simple yet effective dual-memory feature adapter, where a text-memory expands semantic capacity for low2high appearance changes, and a hint memory supplies layer-wise visual feature corrections of high-cost element before context injection. Extensive experiments and ablation studies demonstrate the superiority of CineCraft-120K for low-to-high-cost video editing, alongside the effectiveness of our dual-memory adapter.

[CV-228] Learning to Group and Order: Cross-Instance Self-Supervised RL for Vision-Centric MLLM s NIPS2026

作者: Songming Yang,Hong-Tao Yu,Xiu-Shen Wei

Abstract:Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training has become an important paradigm for improving multimodal large language models (MLLMs), especially with automatically verifiable rewards. Self-supervised visual pretext tasks provide such rewards without human annotations. However, existing methods mainly exploit within-instance structure, offering limited supervision for cross-instance discrimination and fine-grained comparison. We introduce Group-and-Order Self-Supervised Reinforcement Learning (GO-SSL), a cross-instance jigsaw framework for vision-centric MLLM post-training. Given two visual instances, GO-SSL mixes their local elements and trains the model to group them by instance of origin while recovering the order within each group, coupling instance-level comparison with spatial, temporal, or geometric structure recovery. This paired formulation turns the same unlabeled data into richer verifiable supervision through diverse pairings, shuffles, and a random-to-hard curriculum. We instantiate GO-SSL mainly on cross-image jigsaw tasks and further extend it to 3D depth and video temporal ordering. Across diverse benchmarks, GO-SSL consistently improves over the base MLLM and prior self-supervised post-training baselines, with clear gains in fine-grained perception and spatial understanding. Further evaluations across model scales and families support its generality. These results suggest that cross-instance comparison provides a useful self-supervised RL signal for improving transferable visual understanding in MLLMs. Code is available at this https URL.

[CV-229] Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00859
作者: Yijie Jin,Yuxuan Liu,Jiajun Xu,Ye Huang,Chuzhi Wang,Jiayang Li,Ruiyang Chen,Chenling Hong,Xu Wang,Zhijie Deng
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Distributed, Parallel, and Cluster Computing (cs.DC)

Abstract:Real-time long-video generation requires continuous output with consistent appearance and natural motion. Existing chunk-wise autoregressive methods face challenges in both generation efficiency and long-video quality: serialized denoising and history-cache refresh require two forward passes even with one-step denoising, and longer rollouts can degrade quality and cause camera drift. We propose Wave Forcing (WF), which co-designs generation, training, and execution for continuous video output with multi-step denoising. WF uses chunk-wise causal attention to access earlier, cleaner chunks before their denoising is complete, and distributes staggered denoising and cache-refresh stages across full-model replicas to achieve 1F1C: one output chunk per concurrent forward round after pipeline fill. To adapt the model to this continuous generation process, we develop a three-stage training procedure that successively introduces mixed-noise denoising, motion supervision, and causal adaptation using self-generated history. To execute this process efficiently, Wave Runtime (WaveRT) uses Wave Parallelism (WP) for early K/V delivery and communication-computation overlap, together with optimized kernels and pipelined VAE decoding. Experiments on Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B show that 5-step WF maintains overall quality comparable to Rolling Forcing while achieving higher Dynamic Degree on both short and long videos. Our system efficiency experiments show that 4-step WF achieves 147.6 DiT FPS and 134.8 end-to-end FPS on eight H200 GPUs, yielding 7.07x the single-GPU end-to-end throughput. In DiT-only tests with matched SageAttention+W8A8 backends, denoising steps, and GPU counts, WP delivers up to 2.53x the throughput of the faster of the Ulysses and Ring context-parallel baselines across six model scales (1.3B-14B).

[CV-230] oward Counterfactual Learning for Selective Re-Examination in Agent ic Visual Search

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00848
作者: Ao Chen,Shengchao Chen,Yan Luximon
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 32 pages, 17 figures, 14 tables

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Visual search over high-resolution images requires a vision-language model (VLM) not only to determine where to inspect, but also whether another observation is warranted before committing to an answer. Existing prompting, demonstrations, and outcome-based reinforcement learning can encourage re-examination, yet do not directly supervise whether it is beneficial at a particular search state. We introduce ReSee, a benchmark of re-examination decisions comprising 3,227 visual-search trajectories and 8,827 explicit commit-or-re-examine decisions, with counterfactual adjudication that distinguishes states where additional inspection is warranted from those where commitment is preferable. Building on this formulation, we propose CARE (Counterfactual Advantage for Re-Examination), a decision-level reinforcement learning method that compares paired continuations under commit and re-examine verdicts from the same search state. Their cost-aware return difference estimates the counterfactual value of an additional observation and is assigned only to the corresponding verdict tokens, providing localized credit for whether search should continue. Experiments expose limited re-examination selectivity in existing VLMs and show that CARE significantly improves accuracy and decision selectivity over GRPO across two backbones, with higher accuracy and fewer visual requests on six unseen OOD benchmarks.

[CV-231] Running a 20B Video Diffusion Transformer on Consumer Hardware: A Deployment and Measurement Report for MiniMax H3 on Apple Silicon

Abstract:We report the end-to-end deployment and measurement of MiniMax H3, a 20.38-billion-parameter video diffusion transformer (DiT) - the count measured from the safetensors headers of the Q8 checkpoint as deployed locally (Section 3.2) - running entirely on consumer Apple Silicon hardware: an Apple Mac mini with M5 Pro chip and 64 GiB of unified memory. Using the official bf16-to-Q8 (8-bit, group size 64) quantization path executed locally on the machine, we produced a working text-to-video pipeline with no cloud dependency. We document the full deployment procedure, including two non-trivial blockers and their fixes, and report measured figures for build time, peak memory, and per-clip render latency across four resolution tiers (Draft 384x640 through Native 768x1344). A 15.08-second 576x1024 clip rendered in 4838.49 seconds with a measured MLX peak of 27.467 GiB. We further operated the system as an unattended production pipeline, completing 17 clips in 26.49 hours with zero render failures. A blind human review of the 17 production clips (generation prompts withheld) averaged 3.12, 3.18, and 2.94 out of 5 for structural integrity, temporal consistency, and visible artifacts. All figures in this report are our own measurements except where explicitly labeled as third-party data. This is a systems/empirical report; we make no claim of model innovation.

作者: T N Rickesh,Pranav Vinodh,Sowmya Kamath S
