Abstract:Multi-camera driving question answering provides a discrete test of vision-language models, but post-training gains can reflect changed selected answers or improved answer extraction. We investigate this distinction within the Gemma model family using archived, task-linked WaymoQA evaluations. A zero-shot diagnostic on 5,519 test questions spans effective-small, mixture-of-experts, unified, and dense checkpoints, with serving differences disclosed rather than interpreted as architecture effects. The strongest controlled evidence is a matched-harness Gemma-4-12B base/GRPO pair: accuracy rises from 73.78% to 75.43%, a gain of 1.65 percentage points with a scene-cluster bootstrap interval of [+0.84, +2.41]. There are 215 improvements and 124 regressions; 213 improvements start from an extractable but incorrect base answer, and only two recover previously unextractable responses. Crossing correctness with extraction state shows why correct noncompliant outputs cannot be counted as prediction errors. Category counts reveal a critical safety asymmetry: routine perception gains (+5.93 pp) mask a regression in safety-critical hazard prediction (-1.82 pp), demonstrating that unweighted outcome rewards can trade off rare edge cases for aggregate accuracy. Reward saturation describes sampled training dynamics rather than an architectural ceiling. A separate archived Gemma-31B thinking comparison yields no detected average improvement, with uncertainty that does not establish equivalence. These results support a modest answer-selection gain for the recorded tuning configuration and a reproducible diagnostic accounting, without attributing corrected labels to specific grounding mechanisms or claiming superiority over matched supervised tuning.

[CV-233] Beyond Temporal Overlap: Consumer-Aware Evaluation of Sign-Language Segmentation across Three Corpora

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00823
作者: Guohou Zhang,Kalin Stefanov
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: Submitted to IEEE FG 2027. 9 pages, 4 figures. Supplementary material included

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Sign-language segmentation divides continuous signing into clips. In this study, the downstream consumer is a frozen recognizer that assigns one sign label to each predicted clip. Existing metrics instead compare predicted clips with manually annotated boundaries. They do not directly measure whether a clip preserves the visual evidence needed by the recognizer or whether the segmenter produces too many clips. We therefore ask whether overlap metrics and this consumer prefer the same segmenter. We evaluate 27 outputs from three segmentation architectures, three random seeds, and three corpora. Controlled boundary edits separate the effect of removing sign evidence from that of adding surrounding context. Overlap predicts recognition on average, but it does not always determine model choice. At the same intersection-over-union, different recognizers can prefer the shorter or the longer clip. The real outputs reveal two operating regimes. On DGS, overlap, recognition, and sequence error select the same model. On BSL, recognition-based selection recovers and recognizes more reference signs but increases word error rate (WER). Dicta-Sign shows the reverse trade-off: WER selection reduces in-vocabulary WER by 31.17 points but misses more recognizable signs. Segmenters should therefore be evaluated on four axes: temporal agreement, reference recovery, clip recognition, and sequence error, rather than on overlap alone.

[CV-234] UniCaMo: Unified Camera and Motion Control for Video Diffusion Models

作者: Long Vu,Tan Ngo,Animesh Karnewar,Amir Habibian,Binh-Son Hua,Hung Bui,Minh Hoai Nguyen,Phong Nguyen
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Graphics (cs.GR)
备注: Qualitative videos are available on our project page: this https URL

Abstract:We present \textbfUniCaMo, an unified framework for joint control of camera and object motion in image-and-text-to-video diffusion models. Given a reference image, text prompt, sparse 3D object trajectories, and a 3D camera trajectory, UniCaMo constructs motion-consistent input noise that directly encodes the desired motion. Our 3D-grounded noise construction combines reference-derived noise propagation with a spherical Gaussian noise representation for newly revealed regions, providing a simple and effective motion prior without requiring reconstruction of unseen scene geometry. UniCaMo requires no architectural modifications or dedicated control modules and can be adapted using lightweight LoRA fine-tuning with low training data volume. Experiments on standard controllable video generation benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art motion controllability and high visual quality with minimal inference overhead.

Abstract:Multi-object image generation in text-to-image diffusion models remains challenging, as existing approaches struggle to reliably generate all objects specified in a prompt. Compositional approaches that generate objects independently often fail to capture the interactions among them, whereas joint generation methods tend to suffer from inter-object interference. In this work, we propose a training-free framework, termed conditional object composition, that relaxes joint generation methods by taking one step back toward compositional approaches. Our framework decomposes the generation of N objects into two stages: it first generates a subset of N-1 objects and then composes the remaining object conditioned on the generated content. To enable effective composition, we adopt an inpainting-based formulation with layout guidance to preserve existing regions and encourage spatially coherent placement. To address the challenge of selecting which objects to generate separately, we introduce an attention-based scoring mechanism based on cross-attention maps and further explore the use of off-the-shelf object detectors. We evaluate our method on multi-object image generation using the widely adopted MS COCO dataset. Experimental results show that our approach achieves competitive or improved performance compared to existing methods, particularly as the number of objects increases. Further studies highlight the importance of the proposed design choices. The source code is available at this https URL

作者: Akram Zaytar,Kemunto Ochwang’i,Caleb Robinson,Girmaw A. Tadesse,Gilles Q. Hacheme,Rahul Dodhia,Inbal Becker-Reshef,Juan M. Lavista Ferres
类目: Machine Learning (cs.LG); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)

Abstract:Government agencies use crop maps to estimate production, monitor food security, and set agricultural policy. These crop maps are usually validated against field labels, but these labels are rarely a random sample of the area the map covers. Field teams tend to label parcels near roads and skip ones that are small or hard to reach, so performance measured on held-out labels mainly describes the places they visited. We call the difference between this reported performance and performance over the whole mapped region the deployment performance gap. To estimate performance over the whole region, we use a weighted form of prediction-powered inference (PPI). The classifier’s predictions on unlabeled points across the region give a first estimate, and its errors on the labeled points correct that estimate, with more weight on labels from under-sampled conditions. We test this in five European regions where crop registers label every declared parcel, so the true performance is known. Simulating six documented collection practices there produces gaps of up to 0.20 macro-F1. On the collection rule that creates the largest gap in each region, 5 km block cross-validation still overestimates macro-F1 by as much as 0.18, while PPI with weights estimated from satellite embeddings reduces the largest error across regions to 0.07. Importance-weighted cross-validation with the same weights does almost as well, so most of the improvement comes from the weights themselves. We also apply the method to three Kenyan datasets that have no region-wide reference labels. For a roadside dataset collected with helmet-mounted cameras, the estimated macro-F1 falls from 0.93 under random cross-validation to 0.61, although the correction relies on a small number of heavily weighted labels. Our code is available at this https URL.

[CV-237] PhoneValue-Bench: A Multimodal Benchmark and Datasets for Consumer Smartphone Recommerce Valuation

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00791
作者: Zihan Deng,Jun Gao
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:As consumer smartphone recommerce scales, buyers must quote binding repurchase prices from seller-uploaded multi-view photos and diagnostic screenshots before devices reach the warehouse. Accurate remote valuation requires fusing noisy cosmetic evidence with identity, battery, lock, and channel risk from screenshots and staff forms, since an error in any modality changes both grade and payout. However, existing multimodal resources mainly target general VLM competence, screen reading, or factory defect detection, and largely overlook staff-aligned trade-in fields, dual appearance/staff ground truth, and executable valuation scorecards. This gap stems from two challenges: (1) the lack of large-scale real trade-in data with audited dual annotations and a compact ranking benchmark kept separate from training labels, and (2) the need to jointly reason over unordered multi-view cosmetics and diagnostic screens under operational deduction rules. To address these challenges, we propose PhoneValue-Bench, a dual-GT evaluation suite with tier-gated scorecards, together with PhoneValue-Corpus, a matched weakly labeled training set of over twenty thousand orders and hundreds of thousands of captioned images. We further present ValueAgent, a staged perception-fusion-valuation reference pipeline aligned with production inspection, plus an executable public scorer and submission schema. Experiments show that ValueAgent reaches a measured 84.1/100 on Bench-Full, with 97.0 appearance fill and 54.1 staff-field fill, establishing a practical dual-GT benchmark for multimodal recommerce valuation.

[CV-238] Now You See Them Now You Dont FusionGhost Gait for Occlusion-Robust Gait Recognition with ArabGait dataset

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00780
作者: Seba Al Mokdad,Tamer Shanableh,Reham Mohamed Aburas
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: Submitted to “Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence”, Elsevier

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Skeleton-based gait recognition is generally more robust to appearance changes than pixel-based methods, but this robustness depends on stable pose extraction. Clothing variation in gait recognition includes changes in garments, silhouette, and carried items; under Gulf clothing (Kandoora/Abaya), the dominant failure mode shifts from appearance change to lower-limb pose degradation caused by severe occlusion. To study this regime, we introduce ArabGait, a 45-subject indoor multi-view dataset with four walking conditions across three viewpoints, and show that Gulf clothing lowers mean lower-limb confidence from 0.811 to 0.683 and raises lower-limb failure rate from 7.98% to 17.82%, with ankles most affected. We propose FusionGhost-Gait, a fused spatiotemporal architecture that integrates spatial graph blocks and temporal modeling in one residual unit, removes redundant channel projections, and uses compact temporal Ghost kernels as a lightweight regularization mechanism for pose-noisy trajectories while preserving efficient temporal downsampling. On ArabGait cross-clothing evaluation, including Protocol A and Protocol B, FusionGhost-Gait reaches up to 67.91% Rank-1 while remaining compact (108,970- 133,674 parameters and 0.035-0.052 billion floating-point operations (GFLOPs)), achieving more than 65% fewer parameters and 75% lower FLOPs than existing baselines. These results indicate that the proposed model generalizes effectively to challenging Gulf-clothing conditions while remaining lightweight and deployable for surveillance and access-control biometric systems.

[CV-239] DramaVQA: Probing Detailed Understanding of Ultra-Long TV Dramas

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00769
作者: Xinyue Huo,Pengfei Chen,Jiannan Ge,Kaiwen Duan,Jiacheng Shao,Yunning Cao,Lingxi Xie,Qi Tian
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 36 pages. Project page: this https URL

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Despite recent progress in long-form video understanding, current benchmarks mostly focus on short clips or hour-scale videos. This leaves a major gap in evaluating ultra-long video understanding, where videos often last tens of hours. To bridge this gap, we introduce DramaVQA, a large-scale benchmark built upon long-form TV dramas. Containing approximately 20K question-answering (QA) pairs, the scale of DramaVQA exceeds previous long-video datasets, such as Video-MME and LVBench, by an order of magnitude. Our benchmark has two main features that make it stand out from existing datasets. First, we establish a scalable, LLM-assisted annotation pipeline that uses multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to generate complex questions, followed by strict human checking to ensure high data quality. Second, DramaVQA introduces a multi-level time structure; queries are designed across different video lengths, with the hardest questions requiring overall understanding across the entire drama. Extensive evaluations show that state-of-the-art MLLMs face major challenges when tested on these very long videos, highlighting the need for agentic AI algorithms capable of managing long-term memory. The project is available at this https URL

[CV-240] DADKC: Distribution-Aware Adaptive Differentiated Knowledge Consolidation for Cloth-Hybrid Lifelong Person Re-identification

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00768
作者: Yan Zhang,Minghao Long,Meiqi Wan,Yan Yang,Xin Yuan,Wei Wang,Xiao Wang
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: Accepted by MMM 2027

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Lifelong Person Re-identification (LReID) aims to match the same person using sequentially collected data. In practical long-term deployments, however, the model must handle both domain shifts across cameras and scenes, and irregular clothing changes of the same identity. This gives rise to the Cloth-Hybrid Lifelong Person Re-identification (CH-LReID) task, which demands balancing cloth-relevant and cloth-irrelevant knowledge in streaming data. While existing LReID methods have explored replay-based or distillation-based anti-forgetting strategies, they typically fail to sufficiently model stage-aware domain distributions and cross-stage feature continuity under exemplar-free training. To address this problem, we propose a Distribution-Aware Adaptive Differentiated Knowledge Consolidation (DADKC) framework. The core idea is to enhance the existing Differentiated Knowledge Consolidation (DKC) paradigm with adaptive distribution modeling. To this end, three lightweight modules are designed: (1) an Anchor Pool Adapter (APA) to retrieve learnable anchor cues for refining identity features; (2) a Phase Path Mixer (PPM) to perform stage-aware expert routing for integrating domain-specific distribution paths; and (3) a Stage Bridge Alignment (SBA) module to regularize the continuity of base, anchor, and path representations between adjacent stages. Extensive experiments on the CH-LReID and LReID benchmarks show that DADKC gains 4.1%/4.5% mAP/R1 on Order-1 and 3.6%/3.4% mAP/R1 on Order-2 over the DKC baseline, and lowers weighted forgetting from 2.4%/1.7% to 1.8%/1.4%, while storing neither historical images nor per-image features. The code is available at this https URL.

[CV-241] Old Is Not False: Valid-Time Memory for Interactive Video World Models

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00758
作者: Ziming Wang,Chuyue Gong,Hongliang Cao,Jingmin Zhu,Chutian Wang,Yuheng He,Xiuyu Li
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Machine Learning (cs.LG)
备注: 40 pages, 16 figures, 38 tables

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Interactive video world models draw each frame from a memory bank of earlier frames stamped with their capture times. With frames, weights and noise fixed, reversing the timestamps of two views flips the state that generators of two families draw: they take the newest timestamp as the truth. That reading is right as long as states never return. After an agent undoes an action, the newest view of a region is outdated and the only view of the present is older; memories for changing worlds delete that older view, and memories that keep it hand the generator the past. Temporal databases separate when a record is stored from when its content holds, its valid time. ReDate keeps every frame and dates each retrieved token by its valid time, read from the agent’s action log. The frozen generator then reads a reverted region as one that has just reached a new state, so ReDate needs no training. We prove that trusting the newest timestamp is right exactly when every current view is dated after every outdated one, that without a view taken after the return only the action log tells a reverted region from an up-to-date one, and that a generator able to draw from its own prediction gains more from re-dating than from deletion when the moved tokens keep little weight. After an undo, ReDate raises the share of FAR’s steps showing the current state from 0.36 to 0.62 and HY-WorldPlay’s from 0.003 to 0.19. We also propose a calibrated state metric to test any memory after undos.

[CV-242] SceneBound: How Much Should a Streaming 3D Reconstruction Model Remember?

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00756
作者: Ziming Wang,Chuyue Gong,Chutian Wang,Jingmin Zhu,Hongliang Cao,Yuheng He,Xiuyu Li
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Robotics (cs.RO)
备注: 34 pages, 8 figures, 27 tables

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Streaming 3D reconstruction models keep past video frames in a recurrent state, fast weights from test-time training, or a key-value (KV) cache. Each written frame shifts the coordinate frame of later cameras or occupies GPU memory. Training-free rules decide what to write from a signal of the current frame. How much they write accounts for their mean accuracy: spending the update budget of a gate at uniformly spaced frames, with no signal, matches nine published gates, and the budget bounds the drift of the state wherever the writes fall. We propose SceneBound, a training-free rule that writes a frame only when its predicted camera pose lies at least a fixed radius from every stored keyframe. Its keyframe count stays within a constant factor of the covering number of the visited poses, the fewest views that keep a keyframe near every camera, so the count grows with the places visited and stays flat when the camera returns. In large scenes, SceneBound closes a submap once decoding its first frame again reveals drift. SceneBound uses one radius across four released models and three memory types. In the recurrent state of CUT3R and the KV cache of StreamVGGT, it achieves the lowest mean trajectory error among the published training-free rules we evaluate, in one pass and over nine passes of a scene, where its keyframes grow by 3% to 6%.

[CV-243] SAVIER: Source-Anchored Visual Inspection and Evidence-Guided Repair for Vietnamese Cultural Text-to-Image Generation

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00722
作者: Gia-Huy Thai,Duc-Tien Khong,Trung-Nghia Le
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)
备注: Accepted at SOICT 2026. 11 pages, 1 figure

点击查看摘要

Abstract:We present SAVIER, a training-free, one-pass framework that repairs the depiction of a named Vietnamese cultural entity in a generated image while preserving the scene details requested by the user. The problem is hard because a plausible scene can miss the cues that identify the entity, and prompt-level refinement never inspects the image it produces. SAVIER starts from a Culture-TRIP expanded prompt; a Curator separates source-linked cultural cues from prompt-preservation requirements, a prompt-blind Observer describes the first image, and a Refiner turns the discrepancies into at most three positive instructions before one regeneration with the same seed and a fixed bank of reference photographs. On the 50 bilingual prompts of ViCuP, evaluated with SDXL and FLUX.1-dev against a frozen, human-verified visual contract, SAVIER raises contract fulfillment from 55.6 to 69.6 and from 59.1 to 67.3 over Culture-TRIP and raises CAIRE cultural relevance on FLUX.1-dev. A reference-only ablation that removes the agent repair shows that SAVIER’s photographs account for most of the contract gain; the agent roles add country-level relevance on FLUX.1-dev without lowering adherence to the original prompt under the official VQAScore. Project page: this https URL

[CV-244] Adversarial robustness does not entail human-aligned categorization

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00715
作者: Itay Reznik,Raz Lapid,Moshe Sipper,Tal Golan
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Machine Learning (cs.LG); Neurons and Cognition (q-bio.NC)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Adversarial training can improve some forms of correspondence between artificial and biological vision, but whether robust classifiers acquire human-aligned classification behavior remains unclear. We generated 1,008 controversial stimuli by optimizing latent inputs to a pretrained GAN to elicit high-confidence disagreements between pairs of robust ImageNet classifiers. We compared four adversarially robust ImageNet classifiers - ResNet-101, ViT-B, ConvNeXt-L, and Swin-L - with two-alternative category judgments from 60 participants. We first evaluated each classifier on stimuli optimized to elicit disagreement with another model. Across classifiers, accuracy in predicting individual participants’ single-trial category choices was near chance (48.6-51.3%), whereas majority judgments from other participants predicted responses with 85.0-86.8% accuracy. An analysis incorporating model prediction strength and participants’ reported confidence found weak positive model-human correspondence for the two convolutional models. On stimuli optimized for disagreement between other model pairs, all four robust classifiers predicted human responses above chance but less accurately than predictions based on other participants’ majority judgments; the same pattern held for 17 additional RobustBench models not used in stimulus generation. Across these 17 models, mean model-participant agreement was 67.3%, versus 81.3% mean participant-participant agreement on the same images. These results identify model-specific failures of human alignment and a model-human mismatch that persists across robust classifiers and substantially exceeds disagreement among human observers. Our findings show that adversarial robustness alone does not guarantee human-aligned categorization and suggest that robustness and human alignment should be evaluated as distinct properties of visual recognition systems.

[CV-245] LoD-Loc v4: Towards Generalized Aerial Visual Localization via Panoptic LoD 3D Map Registration

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00704
作者: Shuaibang Peng,Chengming Zhang,Juelin Zhu,Xia Li,Xiaoya Cheng,Zeyu Cui,Shen Yan,Maojun Zhang,Yu Liu
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Aerial visual localization over Level-of-Detail (LoD) 3D Maps has recently gained significant traction due to its global scalability, storage efficiency, and privacy-preserving nature. However, existing methods rely almost exclusively on building elements, which leads to catastrophic localization failures in rural or undeveloped areas where buildings are sparse or non-existent. To address this, we construct a unified Panoptic LoD 3D Map by fusing OpenStreetMap (OSM), Digital Elevation Models (DEM), and LoD assets, reformulating the problem as a panoptic registration task. By parsing the query image into discrete building thing' instances and continuous stuff’ regions comprising road, vegetation, and water, we establish a holistic alignment with this map to robustly optimize the camera pose. To enable reliable panoptic perception, we develop a new automated pipeline that constructs AirPan - the largest aerial panoptic segmentation dataset to date, comprising 85k images with pixel-accurate annotations. This empowers our panoptic segmentation model to exhibit remarkable zero-shot generalization capabilities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LoD-Loc v4 consistently outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines by a significant margin. Most notably, it successfully maintains reliable localization in building-less scenarios, completely overcoming the catastrophic failures of prior building-centric paradigms.

[CV-246] Vision-based Sensing of Urban Environment using Hardware-Software co-design at Scale

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00699
作者: Akshit Gupta,R Venkatesha Prasad
类目: ystems and Control (eess.SY); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: IEEE World Forum for Internet of Things 2026

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Urban environmental monitoring is crucial for climate-adaptive cities, yet current approaches rely heavily on human inspection, overhead remote sensing, or limited terrestrial RGB imagery, thereby lacking comprehensive multispectral perspectives at street level. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces UrbanScapes, an adaptable and flexible hardware-software co-design platform for large-scale, vision-based sensing of urban environments. Built on a modular architecture, UrbanScapes seamlessly integrates multispectral imaging channels, including Red, Green, Blue (RGB), Near-Infrared, and Thermal, to capture multispectral street-level imagery. The system is designed for both opportunistic deployment on bicycles, vehicles, or pedestrians and targeted deployments on municipal fleets, ensuring high spatio-temporal scalability without requiring hardware redesigns. Crucially, the platform utilizes on-device deep learning models to automatically remove personally identifiable information (PII) at the edge, addressing privacy concerns inherent in street-level data collection. By combining this multispectral street-level imagery with overhead multispectral remote sensing imagery, UrbanScapes enables scalable calculation of physics-based environmental indices, providing a foundational tool for advanced citywide analysis.

[CV-247] Density-Aware Calibration for Resource-Efficient Medical Vision-Language Models

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00684
作者: Tien-Dat Dam,Huu-Thuan Huynh,Minh-Triet Tran,Trung-Nghia Le
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 15 pages, 2 figures. Accepted at SOICT 2026

Abstract:Medical vision-language models (VLMs) show promise for clinical image understanding, but their computational and memory requirements hinder deployment on resource-constrained clinical hardware. Post-training quantization (PTQ) offers a practical compression strategy without retraining, yet its effectiveness depends strongly on the calibration data. We propose CoreCalib, a training-free and quantizer-agnostic framework for constructing compact calibration sets that preserve the target medical VQA distribution. CoreCalib stratifies data by clinical question class, identifies representative visual modes using frozen DINOv2 features with UMAP and HDBSCAN, and expands selected images into class-balanced question-answer pairs. On Kvasir-VQA-x1, we evaluate CoreCalib with MASQuant, GPTQ, and QIG using a fixed 128-pair budget. CoreCalib achieves the best METEOR with all three quantizers and the best ROUGE-L with MASQuant and GPTQ. With W4A8 MASQuant, it improves METEOR from 0.5672 with COCO calibration to 0.6234, recovering approximately 41% of the degradation relative to BF16. These results support CoreCalib as a data-centric component for resource-efficient medical VLM deployment. Project page: this https URL .

[CV-248] Content-Preserving Principal Feature Blending for Training-Free Style Personalization

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00683
作者: Le-Hoang Bui,Hoang-Nguyen Cao,Trung-Nghia Le,Minh-Triet Tran,Dinh-Khoi Vo
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Reference-based style personalization should reproduce the appearance of a style reference while preserving the subject specified by a content prompt. In visual autoregressive models, dominant reference features can also carry object and spatial information, causing content leakage. We propose Content-Preserving Principal Feature Blending (CoPFB), a training-free method that estimates a low-rank content basis from a clean generation branch and removes the content-aligned component of the style residual. CoPFB applies rank-one blending at the first two autoregressive scales, followed by weaker content-projected refinement at the next three scales. On 1,900 combinations of Parti content prompts and FineStyle reference images, CoPFB improves text alignment from 0.293 to 0.297 and the harmonic score from 0.391 to 0.393 over PFB+SAC, while style similarity decreases from 0.590 to 0.577. CoPFB requires no fine-tuning or learnable parameters. Project page: this https URL.

[CV-249] ROD-Dataset: A Pedestrian-Perspective Benchmark of Urban Obstacle Classes for YOLO-Based Detection

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00681
作者: Abtin Zandi,Ariyan Azami,Bardia Sabagh Kermani,Parsa Abbasian,Roza Ganjipour,Sarvin Nami,Hamed Farbeh
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Computers and Society (cs.CY)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Two groups of pedestrians face avoidable risk on the city sidewalk: people living with visual impairment, who reach an obstacle before anything warns them, and people walking with divided attention, who register a hazard late or not at all. A vision system can warn them only about obstacles it has learned to recognize, so its training data limits the protection it offers. No suitable training set exists: public benchmarks are recorded from vehicles, aerial platforms, or fixed rigs, general-purpose detectors omit the street furniture that causes trips, and pedestrian-focused collections are confined to single regions with incompatible class schemes. This paper introduces the Real-time Obstacle Detection (ROD) dataset: more than 24,000 images and 40,000 annotated obstacles across 25 classes, from vehicles and people to the stairs, manholes, traffic cones, and benches that general-purpose detectors overlook. Because street furniture differs between cities, ROD unifies twenty-nine public collections onto one taxonomy and adds eye-level imagery from two contrasting cities on two continents, Tehran and Toronto. Every label is human-verified, and each capture campaign is admitted only after a compact detector shows it can learn the class. Six lightweight YOLO detectors (nano and tiny variants) benchmarked on ROD all exceed 0.86 recall; YOLO12n attains the highest recall (0.889), YOLO26n the highest precision (0.925), and YOLOv9t the best mAP@0.50 (0.882) with the fewest parameters. Because the recall and mAP rankings disagree, selecting a model by mAP does not minimize missed obstacles, so per-class recall is reported for all 25 classes.

[CV-250] Smooth bounding box for object detection

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00676
作者: Chao Zhou,Shenghua He,Fengchuang Xing,Han Yang,Qiangguo Yu
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Deep learning-based object detection models are highly dependent on the quality of annotated training data. However, large-scale datasets often contain inevitable label noise, with bounding box localization errors being a prevalent and impactful form in object detection. While label noise handling techniques are well-studied for image classification, their adaptation to the more complex problem of bounding box errors remains underexplored. To address this, we propose a novel Smooth Bounding Box (SBB) strategy to mitigate the adverse effects of bounding box annotation inaccuracies. Our key insight is that annotation errors are often linked to annotator factors rather than specific image content, allowing for a statistical correction approach. Based on object size distribution within datasets, we implement the SBB strategy through two methods: 1) Global Scaling Correction (GSC), which applies a uniform scaling factor to estimate and correct a global average error; and 2) Interval Scaling Correction (ISC), which categorizes objects by size into intervals and estimates a dedicated correction factor for each, enabling more precise, fine-grained calibration. For efficient optimization of multiple parameters in ISC, we design a tailored model fine-tuning strategy. Furthermore, we introduce a Normalized Residual Fluctuation (NRF) metric to quantitatively assess the smoothing effect and training stability. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that our method consistently enhances detection accuracy across various model architectures. Both GSC and ISC achieve significant performance improvements over strong baselines, including the latest YOLOv11n, without adding inference overhead. The codes are available at this https URL.

[CV-251] SE-Mem: Semantic-Episodic Memory for Scene-Consistent Generative View Synthesis

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00658
作者: Changsong Lei,Yihan Li,Yu-Hui Wen,Huankun Sheng,Ming Li,Yeying Fan,Minnan Luo,Yong-Jin Liu
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 13 pages, 6 figures

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Generative view synthesis aims to synthesize novel-view videos from reference observations along user-defined camera trajectories. Maintaining global scene consistency throughout this process remains challenging for camera-conditioned interactive video generators. Existing approaches typically select reference frames based solely on camera poses, overlooking whether the content remains semantically relevant or even visible. To address these limitations, we draw inspiration from semantic and episodic memory in human cognition, in which semantic memory captures generalized knowledge across experiences, whereas episodic memory preserves information tied to specific past events and contexts. Motivated by the complementary roles of semantic and episodic memory, we introduce SE-Mem, a Semantic-Episodic Memory framework that organizes historical observations in a structured 3D representation and augments its elements with semantic importance scores. A two-stage memory retrieval strategy is designed to identify the most informative frames to provide contextual guidance. Taking into account both semantic significance and geometric visibility, SE-Mem preserves semantic coherence and fine-grained visual details during novel view synthesis. Extensive evaluations show that our approach improves visual quality and achieves competitive geometric consistency across multiple benchmarks.

[CV-252] Regularized Wasserstein Distance for Discrete Generative Modeling and Clustering Analysis

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00653
作者: Senmao Ye,Fei Liu,Dawei Zhang,Yuqian Zheng,Jun Zhang,Zhonglong zheng
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Machine Learning (cs.LG)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:In this paper, we formulate clustering analysis as discrete generative modeling. Specifically, when the generator is restricted to a finite candidate space, the generated samples naturally emerge as the most representative prototypes of the underlying data distribution. To model such a discrete candidate space, we employ a Discrete Distribution Network (DDN). However, DDN suffers from unstable training due to its hard nearest-neighbor selection. To stabilize training and encourage geometric consistency, we replace DDN’s l2 loss between images with regularized Wasserstein distance between the empirical distributions of real and generated images. The resulting framework, termed Discrete Generative Clustering (DGC), offers four notable advantages: 1) the learned cluster centers are directly interpretable, as they are realistic synthetic samples; 2) the inference cost scales logarithmically with the number of clusters, i.e., O(log K), making the method scalable to extremely large K; 3) the regularized Wasserstein distance provides a smooth and well-behaved optimization objective that facilitates stable convergence, whereas DDN’s l2 loss tends to converge to poor local optima; and 4) DGC replaces DDN’s nearest-neighbor selection with random-neighbor selection, which avoids the density shift problem during multi-step forward. Extensive experiments on several benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and desirable properties of DGC. The code is publicly available at GitHub.

[CV-253] PREM: Prediction-Regulated Memory for Robot Manipulation

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00634
作者: Xiao Huang,Ya Zhang,Weidi Xie
类目: Robotics (cs.RO); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 23 pages, 7 figures

点击查看摘要

Abstract:A robot’s next action can depend on recent motion or earlier visual evidence absent from its current observation. A recurrent visual-memory architecture can retain this history in a visual state, but its usefulness depends on what the state represents and how it is updated with new observations. We introduce Prediction-Regulated Memory (PREM), a framework that uses action-conditioned future prediction to guide both memory learning and updating in vision-language-action policies. During training, predicting future visual features provides temporal supervision for memory learning. During execution, PREM compares current visual features with the prediction made at the preceding decision and uses the spatially normalized prediction discrepancy to regulate updates to the visual state at each spatial location. The updated visual state supplies temporal context for action generation alongside current observations. Built on \pi_0.5 , PREM improves average success rate from 9.63% to 20.74% on DOMINO dynamic manipulation tasks and from 14.4% to 83.8% on the RMBench M(1) memory-dependent setting. Further evaluations on LIBERO and LIBERO-Pro show improvements in general manipulation and robustness to spatial perturbations. PREM incurs a mean inference overhead of 7.7 ms on a single NVIDIA H800 GPU.

[CV-254] Words Before Pixels: Selective Modality Routing for Vision-Language Model Unlearning

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00608
作者: Laura Yao,Haochen Zhang,Jinhao Duan,Sijia Liu,Tianlong Chen
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Vision-language model (VLM) unlearning is often treated as an objective-design problem: given multimodal forget data, the goal is to optimize a loss that removes undesirable behavior while preserving retained capabilities. We argue that this view overlooks an equally important data-centric question: how should each forget example be represented before optimization? Existing methods typically keep image-conditioned failures in their original image-text form, implicitly assuming that pixels are the right route for unlearning whenever pixels appear in the input. We challenge this assumption by constructing modality-decomposed versions of VLM benchmarks, enabling controlled comparisons among image-only, text-only, and multimodal representations of the same examples. Our modality-mixing experiments show that unsafe instruction-following behavior is more effectively suppressed through textual representations than through images alone, while purely text-only unlearning can still weaken visual grounding when the target behavior depends on visual evidence. Motivated by this trade-off, we introduce ModRoute, a gradient-guided per-sample modality routing strategy that selectively converts high visual-pressure examples to text-only form while keeping the remaining examples multimodal. Notably, on VLGuard with LLaVA-1.5-7B, ModRoute has the strongest composite unlearning-utility score of 0.847 at \gamma=0.5 , a 2.5% improvement over the best random-switching score and \geq 46% better than pure multimodal or text unlearning. Overall, our results show that effective VLM unlearning depends not only on the objective, but also on the composition and per-sample modality routing of the unlearning data.

[CV-255] Structured Channel Network Pruning with Bi-Sparse Matrix Factorization

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00566
作者: Jingjing Liu,Ziyang Wang,Xianchao Xiu,Wanquan Liu
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Structured channel pruning for convolutional neural networks (CNNs) plays an important role in pattern recognition and deep learning. Nevertheless, existing methods usually calculate channel importance scores based on the magnitudes of individual filters, making it difficult to distinguish shared redundancy from individual channel contributions. To tackle this limitation, we propose a novel structured channel pruning method termed bi-sparse matrix factorization (BSMF). Specifically, BSMF characterizes the convolutional weight matrix as output-channel coefficients over a shared basis with row-wise \ell_2,p -norm and column-wise \ell_2,q -norm regularization terms, respectively. Note that p,q\in[0,1) , which, to our best knowledge, has not been explored in the literature. To solve the resulting non-convex optimization problem, we develop an efficient update scheme built upon the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), in which all subproblems admit closed-form solutions. After that, a compact CNN is obtained by reconstructing the convolutional filters from the learned factors and discarding the redundant channels. Extensive experiments on the CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1K datasets demonstrate that our proposed BSMF achieves significant network compression while maintaining high reconstruction accuracy. [CV-256] Spatial-Spectral Interactive POCS Network for Large-Gap Seismic Data Interpolation

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00556
作者: Baisong Jiang,Chunxia Zhang,Anxiang Di,Xiaoli Wei,Xiangyu Zhao,Deng Xiong,Chuangji Meng
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Large gaps in seismic acquisition disrupt reflection events and hinder spectral recovery. Existing seismic interpolation deep unfolding networks primarily rely on localized spatial priors, limiting their ability to aggregate the global context necessary for reconstructing these extensive missing regions. We propose a spatial-spectral interactive projection-onto-convex-sets network (SSI-POCS) to tackle this severely ill-posed problem. By unfolding the classical iterative solver, our network integrates physical consistency with dual-domain deep priors via learned transforms, soft thresholding, and exact data reinsertion. Within the learned prior, a spatial Restormer branch captures local waveform structures, while a fast Fourier convolution (FFC) branch extracts global context, effectively suppressing incoherent components and enhancing spectral energy concentration in the f-k domain. A dual-domain fusion module exchanges these complementary features via bidirectional channel attention and gated modulation, yielding substantial interpolation improvements. To overcome the severe loss of lateral continuity caused by large gaps, we introduce structural similarity (SSIM) supervision, complemented by focal frequency loss (FFL) and transform consistency constraints to suppress incoherent high-frequency components and regularize training. Experiments on a synthetic salt dome and a North Sea field dataset under 50% random and consecutive trace removal demonstrate the effectiveness of SSI-POCS. It significantly enhances event continuity across large gaps and mitigates artifacts, achieving a 3.285~dB SNR improvement over the best competing method while reducing parameters by 75.66%.

作者: Jiehui Tang,Yunlong Yu,Zhao Wang,Jungong Han

Abstract:Material rebinding aims to transfer the material appearance from a reference image while preserving the target object’s geometry and identity. Existing methods typically struggle to balance material fidelity with structural preservation due to the coupled influence of structural and appearance cues in their visual conditions. We identify role entanglement in the target and reference conditions as a contributing factor the target condition carries both geometry and its original appearance while the reference condition contains material cues alongside object-specific structure. To address this issue, we propose RATR, a training-free material rebinding method built on a diffusion-based image editor that assigns complementary roles to the two conditions and coordinates their influence during denoising. To make the target condition primarily convey structure, we introduce an albedo-resolved surface release mechanism, which suppresses the target’s original surface appearance while retaining geometric cues, yielding a structure-oriented condition for material transfer. On the reference side, the designed material evidence isolation mechanism emphasizes material cues while reducing interference from object-specific structure, yielding a complementary material-oriented condition.

Abstract:Laser doppler vibrometer (LDV) scans can be used to detect defects and cracks in manufactured parts before they are deployed. This work presents a method for reconstructing the steady-state surface wavefield of a three-dimensional part by combining automated robotic manipulation with neural rendering. A six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) robotic manipulator (UFactory xArm6) with an embedded piezoelectric transducer presented an acoustically excited test article to a stationary LDV at a sequence of known orientations, yielding a set of complex-valued 2D scans with poses derived analytically from the arm kinematics rather than from image-based pose estimation. These scans were used to train a novel complex-nerfacto model, a modified Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) pipeline that replaces the standard three-channel RGB output head with a two-channel output. Complex-nerfacto represents the real and imaginary velocity components of a wavefield, preserving the complex measurement without quantization. Reconstructions of a welded aluminum cylinder and a welded T-bracket were evaluated against measured scans using Z-normalized cross-correlation (ZNCC). The complex-valued pipeline achieved a mean ZNCC of 0.60 at held-out viewing angles, compared with 0.28 for a baseline RGB nerfacto model trained on rendered images of the same data. The resulting surface wavefield reconstructions supported defect detection and characterization on complex components. We identify geometry reconstruction from sparse LDV scans as the remaining obstacle to practical deployment.

作者: Xiangpeng Tian,Mingyang Li,Fajing Liu,Xiaofeng Wang,Xiaohai He,Chao Ren
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: Accepted by IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology

Abstract:All-in-one image restoration aims to recover high-quality images from multiple degradation types using a single unified model. Recent methods improve unified restoration with hybrid attention, prompt learning, or routing mechanisms, but generally focus on enhancing degradation adaptivity while employing similar feature modeling strategies across network stages. Consequently, the distinct representation requirements of encoding and decoding under diverse degradations remain insufficiently explored. In this paper, we propose SASFormer, a Stage-Aware Selective Attention Transformer for all-in-one blind image restoration. SASFormer follows a stage-aware design principle: the encoder uses established hybrid channel-spatial attention to build robust content-preserving and degradation-aware representations, while the decoder employs adaptive selective attention for restoration-oriented reconstruction. To address the stage-specific requirements of decoder reconstruction, we develop Adaptive Selective Channel Self-Attention (ASCSA) and Adaptive Selective Spatial Self-Attention (ASSSA), enabling the decoder to dynamically identify restoration-relevant channel responses and spatial contexts. Specifically, ASCSA performs adaptive query-channel selection and attention masking, while ASSSA adaptively integrates spatial attention across multiple window sizes. Compact implicit prompts further modulate the selection process without requiring explicit degradation labels. Extensive experiments on 3-, 5-, and 11-degradation settings demonstrate that SASFormer achieves strong restoration performance with favorable parameter efficiency. Moreover, stage-wise representation analysis and ablation studies provide empirical support for the proposed stage-aware design and the effectiveness of decoder-side adaptive selection.

[CV-260] Selecting or Solving? What Best-of-N Verification Delivers in Video Reasoning NEURIPS2026

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00507
作者: Martin Q. Ma,Yuxiao Qu,Ruslan Salakhutdinov,Louis-Philippe Morency,Paden Tomasello,Juan Pino
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 VLM4WRD workshop

Abstract:Answering a complex question about a long video is a grounding problem: the answer turns on a few seconds of evidence, and vision-language models remain well below human accuracy at finding them. The standard way to spend extra test-time compute on this kind of video reasoning is best-of-N selection: sample several chain-of-thought answers from a fixed model, then let a second model re-watch the video and pick one. Such pipelines are reported by a single headline number, their margin over a majority vote. That number conflates two effects with opposite deployment consequences: the benefit the second model adds by selecting among candidates, and the benefit it would have supplied by solving the question itself. We separate them, measuring the Selection Increment (SI) – selection accuracy minus the same verifier’s accuracy with the candidates withheld – alongside the margin over self-consistency, across five long-video benchmarks. The Selection Increment is largest for the weakest verifiers: a verifier that solves poorly on its own leaves the candidates the most room to help. Beating the majority vote follows the opposite profile: where the vote already sits near its ceiling no verifier we test improves on it; below that ceiling only the strongest do. On Video-Holmes, the two come apart on a single pool of candidates – a weak verifier gains +19.3 points from the candidates yet lands 7.1 points below the vote, while the frontier verifier gains the least and beats the vote. The weakest verifier also shows a failure mode: on EgoSchema it picks by where an option sits in the list rather than by what the video shows. Read as a merit score, SI puts a verifier that fails to beat a majority vote at the top of its ranking; read as an audit, it says which of the two effects a headline number delivers. Code is available at this https URL.

[CV-261] A Straight Line Is Not a Camera Pose: Auditing Short-Clip Pose Benchmarks

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00482
作者: Xinyi Shi
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Robotics (cs.RO)

Abstract:The absolute trajectory error (ATE) is the standard measure of camera-motion accuracy, from SLAM to feed-forward 3D reconstruction. On the common Sintel protocol, a constant-velocity straight line using no images has a lower mean ATE than 10 of 11 recent models re-run with official code. Two properties of ATE’s alignment explain this. First, it maps any constant-velocity prediction onto the best-fitting line through the true path, so the line scores the path’s regression residual. A residual signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) criterion predicts when moving a prediction towards its constant-velocity fit lowers ATE. It gives the outcome for 95% of 1056 model-clip pairs, 98% of 792 held-out pairs and 97% of 1034 ScanNet pairs, and it separates Sintel (median SNR 0.86) from TUM, ScanNet and full-length Bonn and Wild-SLAM (2.7 to 27), where straightening raises every model’s mean ATE. Second, position-only alignment ignores where cameras look: rotating a trajectory by 30 degrees against its orientations leaves ATE unchanged, yet worsens the reprojection of static points for every model on Sintel, TUM and ScanNet in the main setting, and the line, second by mean ATE on Sintel, places them worst by geometric mean: a lower ATE need not mean better geometry. Fitting the alignment’s rotation to the predicted orientations gives pose-anchored ATE, a one-function change in ATE’s units costing 0.17 ms per clip (ATE: 0.11 ms). It ranks every image-free reference below every model on Sintel, tracks the reprojection error under rotation and straightening, where ATE does not (Spearman 0.61 vs. 0.32), largely preserves the models’ order, and ties 10-frame translational relative pose error (RPE) and the discernible trajectory error (DTE) on our rotation and reference tests. Code, predictions and results will be released.

[CV-262] Spatial Uncertainty Analytics for Budget-Limited Inspection of Hyperspectral Scenes

作者: Ritesh Sharma,Yuichi Motai
类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Land-cover maps classified from wide-area hyperspectral surveys are least reliable along class boundaries and in ambiguous regions, so their errors are spatially structured. We study how this structure can direct a limited verification budget: when a low-altitude UAV or a ground crew can visit only a handful of sites, where it should go depends on how classifier uncertainty is arranged across the scene and how a fixed sensor footprint tiles that arrangement. We estimate a per-pixel uncertainty surface from the disagreement of an ensemble of spectral classifiers and select sites by greedy, field-of-view-aware coverage of the uncertainty mass. On seven benchmark scenes, the highest-uncertainty decile of pixels is 2.6 to 7.9 times richer in errors than the scene as a whole, and the coverage greedy covers up to 57% of the classifier’s errors with 15 sites, 1.7 to 18 times as many as uncertainty-agnostic sampling of the same labelled region. A non-overlapping selection of the footprints richest in uncertainty does equally well, so the gain comes from scoring whole footprints by uncertainty mass. The advantage persists under spatially blocked evaluation and with a spectral-spatial classifier, although disagreement then ranks errors less well. It requires restricting the surface to labelled land cover: over the whole scene, disagreement peaks on unlabelled ground, where inspections cannot be scored. The best policy for covering connected high-uncertainty regions depends on the scene and on the threshold that defines them, and Gaussian-process selection covers less uncertainty than the coverage greedy on every scene. The pipeline runs on commodity CPUs.

[CV-263] PRISM-Net: Dynamic Routing Network with VLM-Guided Disentangled Attribute Distillation for Explainable Fine-Grained Product Retrieval

Abstract:Fine-grained visual product retrieval in large-scale e-commerce multimedia systems demands discriminative representations capable of simultaneously resolving macro-level category semantics and micro-level visual attributes such as structural contour (line) and chromatic appearance (color). However, conventional backbones including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision Transformers (ViTs) inherently suffer from feature entanglement and shortcut learning. To learn the micro-level visual attributes without costly manual attribute annotations, we propose phase-routed interpretable semantic mixture-of-experts network (PRISM-Net), an explainable multi-expert architecture that disentangles holistic visual features into disentangled line and color expert pathways governed by a conditional meta-router. In phase 1, we introduce an external VLM-Guided sigmoid semantic distillation mechanism with gradient-detached routing gates, utilizing zero-shot text prompts from SigLIP to supervise specialized structural and chromatic experts. In phase 2, the disentangled expert embeddings are adaptively fused with macro base features via a learned meta-router gate to calibrate category boundaries. Extensive 5-fold cross-validation across 275,454 e-commerce images (18 categories) and full-scale retrieval benchmarks (55,091 queries against a 220,363-image gallery) across SwinV2, ConvNeXt-V2, and DINOv3 demonstrate substantial gains. On SwinV2, PRISM-Net boosts full-fold product mAP@10 from 80.98% to 83.90% (+2.92%), line mAP@10 by +5.74%, and color mAP@10 by +9.12%. Furthermore, unsupervised distribution analysis of the meta-router gate reveals that both ViT and CNN backbones emergently allocate up to 6.8x higher structural line weights to rigid appliances and hardware while dedicating 96% chromatic weight to clothing.

Abstract:Amodal video object segmentation is fundamentally limited by the absence of datasets that combine real-world complexity with precise ground-truth annotations. To address this, we present Real Video Amodal Segmentation (Real-VAS), a new large-scale, zero-shot evaluation dataset built from composited real-image video. We introduce a novel data generation pipeline that enables the creation of programmatically consistent amodal ground truth for real-world footage, in which the object mask, occlusion boundary, and composited image are all derived from a single unoccluded source, without relying on human estimation or expensive 3D reconstruction. Our dataset is structured into two challenging scenarios: dynamic Occlusion, created by compositing two clips of moving objects, and a unique Container category featuring complex, physically constrained interactions. These container scenarios–On Surface Containment, Articulated Containment, and Mobile Containment–allow us to generate precise ground truth by simulating an object’s motion based on its container’s tracked transformation. As a result, Real-VAS provides a diverse and challenging benchmark for evaluating amodal segmentation models on realistic video with the precision of synthetic data. The dataset and our generation code will be made publicly available.

类目: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Cryptography and Security (cs.CR); Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Abstract:Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) have recently emerged as general-purpose visual world models for control. A prominent example is LeWorldModel (LeWM), which trains end-to-end from pixels using an isotropic Gaussian anti-collapse regularizer (SIGReg) and plans by minimizing the squared Euclidean distance between predicted and goal embeddings. In this work, we investigate the test-time robustness of this latent planning interface. Analyzing the learned metric on Push-T, we first find that task-relevant object state heavily dominates latent distance: shifting the block by a single pixel displaces the embedding 3\times further than an equivalent agent shift, and swapping the block pose alone accounts for 99% of the distance between scene pairs. However, because this pose information is distributed across a curved, high-dimensional manifold rather than a fixed linear subspace, the encoder cannot be trivially edited post-hoc to isolate or redirect it. We next demonstrate that this geometry is highly vulnerable at test time. A white-box \ell_\infty perturbation of just \epsilon=4/255 applied to a single input frame causes the encoder to register the block at an arbitrary, attacker-chosen pose in 73 – 95% of scenes without disturbing the encoded agent state. Perturbing either the goal image or the live camera observation drops Push-T planning success from 87% to 32% , whereas uniform random noise at twice the magnitude has negligible impact. This vulnerability persists across all four standard LeWM benchmarks (Push-T, Two-Room, Reacher, and OGBench-Cube). At \epsilon=8/255 , the attack bridges 82 – 97% of the squared latent distance to the target embedding in every environment, inducing planning degradation proportional to each task’s reliance on the spoofed entity.

Abstract:Dense action detection requires precisely localising multiple overlapping actions in long untrimmed videos. We present PAM-Mamba, a linear-time O(T) architecture built on Mamba with a multi-branch temporal encoder. Gated Learnable Positional Encoding (GLPE) controls positional signal injection via a scalar gate initialised to zero, starting training without added positional signal. A Hub-and-Spoke Funnel extends the non-hierarchical multi-scale design of PAT with a direct residual from the original full-resolution input to each coarse branch, providing each coarse branch with a projection of the input features. Bi-TemBa (Bidirectional Temporal Mamba) first extracts local motion cues with a shallow Temporal Convolution Module, then applies a cascaded bidirectional Mamba scan; the backward pass refines the forward-scanned representation from the opposite direction, giving each temporal position access to context from both directions in linear time. Using the PAT evaluation implementation, we obtain 26.82 (Charades I3D), 34.59 (Charades CLIP), 46.56 (MultiTHUMOS I3D), and 46.92 mAP (MultiTHUMOS CLIP), with 26.1-27.9M parameters, 61-63% fewer than PAT.

Abstract:Tracking points that leave the camera’s field of view (FoV) requires reasoning about unobserved scene dynamics, a fundamentally different problem from tracking visible correspondences. We demonstrate its flexibility on out-of-frame object segmentation and detection and we provide detailed diagnostic analyses across motion regimes, static versus dynamic content, and hallucination quality, characterising when and why the approach succeeds or fails.

Abstract:In retinal vessel segmentation, plain Vision Transformers (ViTs) are commonly expected to perform worse than convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on thin vessels, for reasons such as their coarse patch tokenization, their weak locality bias and their need for large training sets. Although this expectation is widely shared in the literature, how plain ViTs actually compare with CNNs on thin vessels has not been systematically quantified. We address this question by comparing a model with a plain ViT encoder (MedSAM), a hybrid Transformer (LiteMedSAM) and three CNNs of different sizes on three retinal datasets (DRIVE, HRF, FIVES) and, as a second-domain check, a microscopy dataset (VessMap). We measured the centerline recall and precision of thin vessels and compared the models while also considering their computational cost and how many epochs they needed to train. We found that the pre-trained MedSAM had a centerline recall of thin vessels that was not significantly different from that of the best CNN on all four datasets (-0.6 to +2.5 percentage points). A compact plain ViT obtained through architecture search but trained from scratch did not retain this performance. For pre-trained plain ViTs, our results do not support the expectation that they miss thin vessels, although similar thin-vessel performance can be obtained with much smaller models.

Abstract:Future dynamic novel-view synthesis requires extrapolating multiple motion regimes within the same scene. A single dynamics model may not simultaneously represent stationary regions, coordinated motion, local interactions, and articulated trajectories. We introduce Motion Regime Expert Routing for Gaussian Splatting (MoRE-GS), a causal, render-aware framework for forecasting dynamic 3D Gaussian scenes. MoRE-GS freezes a Gaussian representation reconstructed exclusively from the observed temporal prefix and forecasts its control-keypoint motion using four complementary experts: persistence, a coefficient-space Transformer, a graph convolutional network, and a structured Transformer with rigid and non-rigid motion constraints. A compact routing table assigns expert mixtures across soft motion groups and forecast-horizon bins, while a persistence gate suppresses unreliable extrapolation. Across D-NeRF and HyperNeRF scenes, MoRE-GS achieves improved performance against other methods, and these results demonstrate that renderer-calibrated composition of complementary motion predictors improves causal dynamic Gaussian forecasting across heterogeneous motion regimes. Abstract:Defense systems for maritime assets must distinguish approaching benign craft from uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) with sufficient warning to act. Shore cameras using computer vision can separate hostile vessels from benign traffic, but these systems may be attacked using an adversarial hull patch or physical disguise. We evaluate adversarial hull patches and find they suppress detection in up to 29% of attempts but never cause misclassification as benign. Physical disguise, however, can bypass both a camera check and a radar presence check. To evaluate defenses, we develop a hybrid replay protocol from automatic identification system (AIS) tracks that combines recorded benign motion with direct or off-axis attack run-ins. We find that for recreational-labeled vessels attacking via direct run-in within 4 nautical miles, an asset-relative closing-rate check flags 94-95% at 15-20 knots, compared with 12% for a track-only speed check. The checks are complementary on off-axis approaches, constraining the attacker to remain below both thresholds and extending the time required to reach the asset. Flagging on either check has a 4.9% held-out false-alarm rate overall and 12.3% on recreational traffic. The replay-based evaluation protocol supports comparative test and evaluation of defense methods.

Abstract:Multi-image vision-language models (VLMs) incur substantial computation when processing long visual sequences. Compressing these sequences must preserve complementary evidence across images and keep tokens from different images separate. Global selection can underrepresent question-relevant images, and pruning in early decoder layers risks removing relevant content before sufficient multimodal processing, yet existing methods spend most of the budget on these early layers. We propose SIEVE, a training-free, single-pass framework that jointly allocates visual tokens across images and decoder depth. SIEVE first pools each image into a compact spatial grid to reduce early processing cost. It then progressively selects representatives using prompt attention under equal per-image quotas and aggregates unselected tokens into similar representatives from the same image. These operations keep every image represented and its tokens separate from other images, while refining the retained representations. A closed-form schedule sets retention counts to target a prescribed average token budget across decoder layers. Across four VLM backbones, SIEVE achieves the highest average at a 6.25% budget on five multi-image benchmarks and four single-image benchmarks, and the highest mean on two video benchmarks. On LLaVA-OneVision-7B, it outperforms the strongest baseline by 9.96 and 9.03 points at 6.25% and 12.5% budgets, and at 12.5% it exceeds the uncompressed model by 2.01 points with 6.6x fewer prefill FLOPs.

Abstract:We propose \emphDéjà Vu, a test-time decoding module for semantic correspondence. Matching semantically equivalent keypoints across images of the same object category is challenging due to variations in appearance, viewpoint, and scale. While features from large pretrained vision models carry strong zero-shot correspondence ability, existing methods reduce final matching to greedy top- 1 nearest-neighbor selection. We show that the correct correspondence appears among the top-ranked candidates far more often than top- 1 matching achieves: with 30 candidates, zero-shot features exceed the top- 1 accuracy of a supervised model. This reveals a \textitdecoding bottleneck rather than a limit of the representation. Motivated by this observation, we formulate semantic correspondence as a \textitrecall-then-rerank problem. Our method first nominates an adaptive candidate set, larger when the similarity distribution is ambiguous and smaller when it is confident, then re-ranks the candidates with a graded cycle-consistency score: each candidate is matched back to the source image and penalized by how far its reverse match lands from the original keypoint. The module operates entirely on the similarity matrix already computed by the base method. It consistently improves three representative baselines on SPair-71k, its geometric subset, and PF-Pascal under both unsupervised and weakly supervised settings, with gains of up to +1.8 PCK@0.10 on SPair-71k and +3.4 PCK@0.15 on PF-Pascal, and +4.9 under Keypoint Average Precision.

作者: Mingyang Bao,Fangda Ye,Xihao Chen,Bobo Li,Jason Li,Shengqiong Wu

Abstract:Recent advances in video generation have achieved impressive visual quality, yet they often fail to produce physically consistent dynamics due to the lack of explicit modeling of underlying physical processes. Existing approaches either rely on simulators with strong assumptions or use coarse semantic guidance, and further struggle to effectively inject physical priors into generation models. In this work, we propose Seeing the Unseen, a unified framework for physics-grounded video generation. Our approach decomposes the problem into two stages: learning physical dynamics and injecting them into video synthesis. First, we introduce a lightweight Particle-based Graph Dynamics Simulator (PGDS) that learns generalizable physical interactions from data and predicts plausible 3D motion trajectories. Second, we propose a Visible–Invisible Motion Field (VIMF) that captures both motion observable in the input frame and motion that emerges over time due to object dynamics. This representation enables more complete and structured motion guidance compared to conventional physical signals. By integrating these trajectories into a diffusion-based generator, our method produces videos that are both visually coherent and physically consistent. Extensive experiments demonstrate improved motion accuracy, interaction consistency, and reduced physical artifacts compared to strong baselines.

Abstract:Cross-view geolocalization aims to determine the geographic location of a ground-level image by retrieving its corresponding satellite image, offering a promising alternative for localization in Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)-denied or degraded environments such as urban canyons, dense forests, and disaster scenarios. Despite recent progress, existing approaches remain limited by the lack of globally diverse training datasets and benchmarks that are often geographically restricted. Furthermore, most benchmarks rely on panoramic ground views, which do not reflect the limited field-of-view imagery captured by real world cameras. To address these challenges, we introduce Cross-View World 500k (CVW500k), a large-scale globally distributed dataset containing over 500,000 ground-satellite image pairs collected across diverse geographic regions and environments. Unlike previous datasets, CVW500k uses limited field-of-view ground images, providing a more realistic and challenging setting for cross-view geolocalization. In addition, we propose GeoQueryNet, a query-based cross-view fusion transformer framework designed to bridge the viewpoint gap between ground and satellite images. The model leverages a CLIP-based visual encoder with parameter-efficient LoRA adaptation and introduces a Cross-View Alignment Module that uses learnable query tokens to extract geographically consistent features across viewpoints. Our code can be found here: this https URL . Abstract:Converting a raster image into a resolution-independent, stroke-editable vector sketch while faithfully preserving both structural contours and tonal texture remains challenging: raster-space rendering pipelines are difficult to edit at the stroke level, while generation-from-scratch vectorization methods struggle to remain faithful to an arbitrary input image. We present SketchForge, a training-free framework that converts an input raster image into a resolution-independent SVG sketch through per-instance test-time optimization of Bezier curves, requiring no additional training or fine-tuning. Strokes are seeded via a contour and attention-guided initialization, then refined by a vector-native differentiable rendering pipeline that decouples structural contour strokes from free-form texture strokes under dedicated objectives, composited via multiply-blend layering. Extensive experiments show that SketchForge consistently outperforms existing vector-based baselines in structural fidelity and generation quality. Project page: this https URL

[CV-276] aurus: LLM -in-the-Loop CT Annotation Matches Coding Agents at Half the Cost

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00247
作者: Bing Hu,Rishabh Sharma,Jatin Mehta
类目: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)
备注: 24 pages (10 main text, 12 appendix), 8 figures, 10 tables

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Dense labels of the aorta in CT are slow to draw, and the public aortic CT datasets that could stand in for them each label different structures under their own conventions. Large language model (LLM) agents can now write code and read images. We asked whether such a model labels these scans better as a free-form agent that writes its own segmentation code, or inside a harness, where an automated pass labels the scan and the model reviews the result. We built a harness, Taurus, and compared it with free-form agents by blind label recovery: we withheld the human labels of six public datasets (939 volumes) and scored every approach against each dataset’s own classes. In the first version of Taurus, the model’s review raised the primary metric on only two of six datasets, by less than the noise between two reviews of the same case. A free-form agent running Claude Opus 5.5 scored higher on most datasets. Moving what the free-form agents did well into the automated pass then carried most of the gain on 38 held-out cases. The final version smooths the label surfaces with a fixed rule and checks for the large errors the automated pass tends to make, such as an aneurysm drawn to half its size. Each check that fires puts a multiple-choice question to the model, with candidate corrections drawn on the scan. It matched the surface smoothness of the human references, and in the primary metric we found no difference from the free-form Opus agent, at under half its cost, 1.22 against 2.71 per case. Most of what made Taurus competitive came from the harness and its automation rather than from the language model itself. Taurus shows that this kind of annotation can be automated, so that expert time can move from drawing labels to checking them.

Abstract:Outpainting sparse sketches while preserving contour coherence and stroke style remains challenging. We present SketchBloom, a training-free framework that combines pretrained raster outpainting and style-transfer guidance with per-instance vector optimization. Given a sketch, a scene prompt, and an optional reference style, it produces an editable Scalable Vector Graphic (SVG) composed of Bezier strokes. Adaptive latent blending balances content contours and reference texture without model retraining. A reference-derived stroke vocabulary initializes contour- and DINO-attention-guided strokes, which are optimized separately for structure and texture before contour-emphasizing multiply fusion. As in prior optimization-based vector sketching, no task-specific network is trained; our contribution is the synthesis design specialized to sketch outpainting. On LineArtOut-1K, comprising 1,024 input and style combinations, SketchBloom improves perceptual, semantic, and structural fidelity over the evaluated vector baselines when all methods vectorize the same outpainted raster. This protocol evaluates vector synthesis rather than end-to-end outpainting or reference-style superiority. Runtime is approximately six minutes per pair on a single NVIDIA H200 GPU. 作者: Yizhou Liu,Zhengxi Lu,Fei Tang,Yiwen Qiu,Yong Du,Tongbo Chen,Bofan Chen,Tao Jiang,Wenhao Xu,Yunfeng Shu,Wenqi Zhang,Weiming Lu,Jun Xiao,Yueting Zhuang,Yongliang Shen

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Existing Graphical User Interface (GUI) benchmarks predominantly rely on precise and stateless user instructions. In everyday usage, however, instructions are often \emphvague and history-dependent: users omit the exact details of their past operations because they no longer remember them, leaving the agent to recover the missing context from long and noisy interaction histories. To bridge this evaluation gap, we introduce \textbfMemU-Bench, a mobile benchmark of \textbf118 vague tasks grounded in 29 long-horizon user trajectories, where agents must distill raw interaction streams into memory and retrieve the missing context on demand, with task outcomes verified against serialized application databases. Alongside Success Rate, we incorporate Interaction Efficiency (IE) and Success weighted by Path Length (SPL) to expose agents that succeed by exhaustively searching across different applications rather than by \emphgenuinely recalling the history. Evaluations show that without user history, state-of-the-art systems struggle under such ambiguity: the best-performing Gemini-3.1-Pro achieves an SPL of only 16.4%, and end-to-end GUI agents fall below 5%. To address this, we further propose \textbfAppMem, a training-free framework that distills user history into a \emphstructured, app-centric memory bank, tracks interrupted intents across application switches, and selectively retrieves relevant memories via target-app inference. AppMem raises the SPL of GPT-5.5 from 15.7% to 66.9% (\textbf+51.2%), outperforms a naive summary baseline by 9.3%, and delivers consistent gains across evaluated backbones.

[CV-279] Learning to Live: A Step Toward Lifelong Embodied Intelligence

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00180
作者: Lirong Che,Peidong Wang,Yimeng Su,Jiong Wang,Yang Chen,Wenbo Fu,Zhenyu Huang,Tiancheng Xu,Yuzhe Yang,Dongli Xie,Xu Cao,Chuang Wang,Daqi Liu,Jian Su

备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Embodied agents are usually organized around individual tasks, yet the physical world keeps changing between tasks and during execution. We introduce LIFE (Lifelong Intelligence from Experience), a framework in which a robot observes continuously, remembers selectively, and turns experience into new capabilities. RoboBeats, a family of lightweight streaming gates, tracks conditions set by the agent and discovers new events, deciding when an observation warrants a response or a memory write. Selected observations enter Plastic Memory, a flat store of images and structured records that keeps the source evidence, so new fields and indexes can be added when later questions need them. When existing tools fall short, Explore-Distill-Mount (EDM) turns solutions found during problem solving into validated, reusable tools and skills. Under matched protocols, RoboBeats substantially improves condition tracking over its base models and, at the same writing budget, retains more useful evidence for memory question answering than uniform sampling. A case study of limited scale, replaying 24 hours of continuous video recorded by a real robot, illustrates how the integrated system builds memory from a day of experience and uses it to answer everyday questions. LIFE takes a step toward robots that become more familiar with their surroundings and more capable through experience: learning not only to complete tasks, but to live in the world.
